384YE Summer Solstice Imperial elections.d: National elections returned senators for Bastion (Ehud), Karov (Vuk The Wolfeater), Miaren (Llewellyn Leafstalker), Mitwold (William Lowther), Redoubt (Sejanus), Sarvos (Shauni di Vergo), Sermersuaq (Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason) and Weirwater (Baldwin). The Senate appointed Jarrigk Orzel as Imperial Consul and named generals for ten armies, among other posts. The Synod chose Lady Clarice Novarion as Cardinal of Courage and Hembeneth i Guerra as Cardinal of Wisdom, plus inquisitors and other religious titles. Bourse auctions and votes settled ministries such as the Night Quarry (540 thrones) and the Mistress of the Glass Parador. Cadogan Stranger's Song became Grandmaster of the Order of the Unfettered Mind.

n.Dawn: Dawn returned Baldwin as Senator for Weirwater in its national election at this summit.
n.Highguard: Highguard returned Ehud as Senator for Bastion in its national election at this summit.
n.Navarr: Navarr returned Llewellyn Leafstalker as Senator for Miaren in its national election at this summit.
n.The League: The League returned Shauni di Vergo as Senator for Sarvos in its national election at this summit.
n.The Marches: The Marches returned William Lowther as Senator for Mitwold in its national election at this summit.
n.Urizen: Urizen returned Sejanus as Senator for Redoubt in its national election at this summit.
n.Varushka: Varushka returned Vuk The Wolfeater as Senator for Karov in its national election at this summit.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark returned Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason as Senator for Sermersuaq in its national election at this summit.

t.Bastion: Ehud was elected Senator for Bastion, taking up its seat in the Imperial Senate.
t.Karov: Vuk The Wolfeater was elected Senator for Karov, taking up its seat in the Imperial Senate.
t.Miaren: Llewellyn Leafstalker was elected Senator for Miaren, taking up its seat in the Imperial Senate.
t.Mitwold: William Lowther was elected Senator for Mitwold, taking up its seat in the Imperial Senate.
t.Redoubt: Sejanus was elected Senator for Redoubt, taking up its seat in the Imperial Senate.
t.Sarvos: Shauni di Vergo was elected Senator for Sarvos, taking up its seat in the Imperial Senate.
t.Sermersuaq: Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason was elected Senator for Sermersuaq, taking up its seat in the Imperial Senate.
t.Weirwater: Baldwin was elected Senator for Weirwater, taking up its seat in the Imperial Senate.

384YE Summer Solstice Senate sessions.d: The Senate amended the Liberty Pact to add an embargo on Jarm and free trade between signatories. It created the Imperial Administrator, Imperial Warcaster, Spiral Envoy and Archivist of the Echoing Obelisk titles, and stripped the Warmage of arranging magical assistance for armies. It disbursed 150 thrones for the Towerjacks and 55 thrones 6 crowns for William Lowther's resupply. The first raid motion failed and the second passed; the raid later succeeded. Nine commissions passed, including Ratibor's Gate Shrine, the White Roads and the Zemress Naval Academy, alongside wayleave projects such as Greenwood Manor. An appraisal of a non-human Throne failed.

n.Dawn: Jarrigk Orzel of Dawn was elected Imperial Consul, and Greenwood Manor in Semmerholm creates two titles elected by the Dawnish National Assembly. Astolat secured 150 thrones for the Towerjacks.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Highwatch Citadel expansion will provide vis and pearls to enchant an Imperial army attacking the Druj.
n.Highguard: The Highguard National Assembly will appoint the new Archivist of the Echoing Obelisk. The White Roads of Virtue's Path and the Garden of the Imperial Auxiliaries were commissioned in Highguard territories.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's senator seconded the Angelica Memorial House of Healing, and Skarsind is noted as relinquished by Wintermark in 380YE.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Pride of Ikka's Tears is noted as having been lost to the Empire in war with the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Navarr gained a bladeroot sinecure in Hercynia, whose Steward of the Nabarr is appointed by Navarr senators, and a fortified steading at Mudlark's Haven in Therunin.
n.The Brass Coast: The Zemress Naval Academy was commissioned in Madruga, and a wayleave created the Crimson Sutannir title, elected by the Brass Coast National Assembly. Brass Coast senators also proposed the Archivist title and the successful raid motion.
n.The League: League senators won commissions for Ratibor's Gate Shrine in Temeschwar, the Blood Red River Museum in Tassato, the walls of Holberg and a House of Healing in Sarvos, creating several League-appointed titles.
n.The Marches: Watt of Lambrook was elected Advisor for the Feni, and 55 thrones 6 crowns went to Senator Mitwold for William Lowther's resupply. The Marchers' proposal to appraise a non-human Throne failed.
n.Urizen: Urizen senators created the Spiral Envoy, though its appointment by them was ruled unconstitutional. A wayleave created the Polemarch of Highwatch, elected by Urizen senators.
n.Varushka: Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti was elected Minister of Historical Research and sent researchers to the Palace of Orieb. Karov's first raid motion failed, while Ossium proposed the Imperial Warcaster.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark was reassigned the territory of Sermersuaq and given the Pride of Ikka's Tears as its sole national bourse seat.

t.Astolat: Astolat's senator proposed and received 150 thrones from the treasury to improve the Towerjacks.
t.Bastion: The White Roads of Virtue's Path will run through Bastion, whose senator also proposed amending the Warmage's duties.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea's senator proposed the White Roads commission and seconded Ratibor's Gate Shrine.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark's senator proposed allocating the Pride of Ikka's Tears and seconded assigning Sermersuaq to Wintermark.
t.Hercynia: A bladeroot sinecure was commissioned at Old Ranging in Hercynia, creating the title of Steward of the Nabarr.
t.Holberg: The Senate commissioned fortification of Holberg's walls, funded by its own citizens. Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg also donated 28 thrones to the treasury.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman's senator proposed the Zemress Naval Academy and seconded the Liberty Pact amendment.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov's senator proposed the failed first Asavean raid motion and seconded the Minister of Historical Research appointment.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk's senator proposed the appraisal of an Architectural University and seconded the failed first raid motion.
t.Madruga: The Zemress Naval Academy, a self-funded school of naval warfare, was commissioned in Madruga, and a liao sinecure was announced for its Torres region.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren's senator seconded the Warmage amendment and proposed the Imperial Consul appointment.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova's senator seconded the Architectural University appraisal and proposed the Minister of Historical Research appointment.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold's senator proposed and received 55 thrones 6 crowns for William Lowther's resupply, and seconded the bladeroot sinecure.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow's senator proposed ceding the Eleonaris statue and seconded the Spiral Envoy.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold's senator proposed the failed non-human Throne appraisal and seconded the resupply funds.
t.Necropolis: The Garden of the Imperial Auxiliaries was commissioned in Coursmouth, and the White Roads will pass through Necropolis.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium's senator proposed the Imperial Warcaster and seconded the Sodality, and the Eleonaris statue honours victories in Ossium.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's senator proposed the Spiral Envoy and seconded ceding the Eleonaris statue.
t.Reikos: The White Roads will extend into Reikos, whose senator also proposed the Liberty Pact amendment and seconded the successful raid motion.
t.Sarvos: A House of Healing sinecure in memory of Angelica Vergo di Sarvos was commissioned in Riposi to grow herbs for the League. It remains under additional scrutiny.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura's senator proposed the successful Asavean raid motion and seconded the Archivist title.
t.Semmerholm: Greenwood Manor will be built and the Greenwood Market renovated in Semmerholm. A statue to Eleonaris will stand at its end of the Golden Causeway.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's senator seconded the Sarvos House of Healing, and Skarsind is noted as relinquished by Wintermark in 380YE.
t.Tassato: The Senate authorised rebuilding the Blood Red River Museum in Tassato, creating the Curator of the Blood Red River. There is concern that the title would grant Synod votes.
t.Temeschwar: Ratibor's Gate was to be consecrated with an inspirational tomb and a Watcher of Ratibor's Torch. An appraisal of an Architectural University in Temeschwar was also commissioned.
t.Therunin: A fortified steading called Mudlark's Haven was commissioned in the Feverwater.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's senator proposed the Feni advisor appointment, and the Old Morgan under research may have come from Upwold.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Volodmartz's senator proposed the lineage Sodality and seconded the Holberg walls commission.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater's senator proposed reassuring the Great Forest Orcs over the Heart of Peytaht and seconded the Towerjacks funding.

r.Madruga/Torres: A wayleave announced the Crimson Drummers sinecure in Torres, funded by Ahraz i Guerra, to produce liao and Synod votes under a tenured Crimson Sutannir.

384YE Summer Solstice interlude.d: The 350-throne Guerdon was shared among units supporting the Green Shield, Wolves of War, Citadel Guard and the Feroz, Isember and Hotters Mire opportunities. Military units and fleets could stealthily evacuate citizens from Feroz to Segura and Madruga, raid Jotun-held Skallahn, fight the Isember bandits troubling southern Karsk and Ossium, surround the Feni settlement of Hotters Mire in Liathaven, or venture into the Twisted Woods. Navarr, Dawn, the Brass Coast, Urizen and Varushka disavowed the Skallahn raid. Other effects included mana site disruption from the hunt for followers of Yaw'nagrah, Highborn congregations aiding the fight against the vallorn, congregation bonuses from the Reject False Gods mandate, and the Sand Fisher tithe in Holberg.

n.Dawn: Dawnish units supporting Dawnish, Highborn or Navarr armies engaged in Dark Ranging gained an extra crown and two herbs until the Winter Solstice 384YE, and were among the most effective in the Twisted Woods. Dawn disavowed the Skallahn raid, halving its units' effectiveness there but sparing the nation any penalty.
n.Grendel: The Grendel held Feroz, and the Imperial evacuation of citizens from the territory was a stealthy mission designed to avoid conflict with them wherever possible.
n.Highguard: Thanks to the Three Watchers, Highborn military units could be upgraded for one fewer wain of mithril until the Autumn Equinox. Highborn congregations produced two fewer votes and one fewer liao but could aid any opportunity to fight the vallorn.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were the target of a surprise Imperial raid on Skallahn. For every 10,000 strength committed, they would be unable to provide emergency resupply to their armies for one season.
n.Navarr: Units that had fought to protect Hercynia and Therunin were still recovering from casualties until the Summer Solstice. Navarr disavowed the Skallahn raid, and Navarr armies engaged in Dark Ranging could draw boosted Dawnish support.
n.The Brass Coast: Imperial units and fleets could help evacuate citizens from Feroz to safety in Segura and Madruga. The Brass Coast disavowed the Skallahn raid.
n.The League: Congregations in Tassato and Temeschwar gained two votes and one liao while the Synod opposed idolatry. Farms in Holberg received herbs from the Sand Fisher orcs.
n.Urizen: Urizen disavowed the Skallahn raid. Aspect of the Mountain, Crown of Phoenix Fire and A Perfect Moment were added to Urizen lore, and congregations in Redoubt gained extra votes and liao.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan National Assembly urged every unit not supporting an army or fortification to tackle the Isember bandits, halving the effectiveness of other actions. Varushkans were also most effective in the Twisted Woods and disavowed the Skallahn raid.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark fleets could support the Skallahn raid at full effectiveness, and congregations in Hahnmark gained two votes and one liao under the Reject False Gods mandate.

t.Brocéliande: The vallorn of Brocéliande had become quiescent but remained a threat. Dawnish units supporting armies engaged in Dark Ranging there earned extra rewards, and Highborn congregations were encouraged to keep opposing it.
t.Feroz: Imperial military units and fleets could join a stealthy evacuation of citizens unable to reach the coast, avoiding the occupying Grendel as much as possible.
t.Hahnmark: Congregations in Hahnmark gained two extra votes and one extra liao as long as the Synod stood clearly against idolatry, following the forcible redesign of Asavean-designed buildings.
t.Hercynia: Units that had fought to protect Hercynia suffered a two-rank penalty while recovering, lasting until the start of the Summer Solstice.
t.Holberg: Farms in Holberg received two random herbs each season as a tithe from the Sand Fisher orcs.
t.Karsk: The Isember bandits threatened the vales of southern Karsk, and military units could fight them and claim their loot. Karsk congregations also gained two votes and one liao under the Reject False Gods mandate.
t.Liathaven: Scouts of the Liathaven spy network uncovered an opportunity to surround the Feni settlement of Hotters Mire, rewarding participating units with spring vis.
t.Madruga: Madruga was one of the places of safety for citizens being evacuated from Feroz.
t.Ossium: Settlement of Ossium was being impeded by the Isember bandits. If the Tower of the Manticore were built there, the Into the Twisted Woods action would become permanently available to Dawn and Varushka.
t.Redoubt: Congregations in Redoubt gained two extra votes and one extra liao while the Synod maintained a clear anti-idolatry stance.
t.Segura: Segura was one of the places of safety for citizens being evacuated from Feroz.
t.Skallahn: The Empire could launch a surprise raid into Skallahn, taking metals, forest materials and bourse resources. The Marcher assembly urged raiders to focus on military targets.
t.Tassato: Tassato congregations gained two votes and one liao under the Reject False Gods mandate, enacted by Rafael Barossa di Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Congregations in Temeschwar gained two extra votes and one extra liao while the Synod maintained a clear stance against idolatry.
t.Therunin: Units that had fought to protect Therunin suffered a one-rank penalty while recovering, lasting until the start of the Summer Solstice.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Under Ranae deRondell's mandate, Dawnish units supporting a Dawnish, Highborn or Navarr army engaged in Dark Ranging gained an extra crown and two random herbs until the Winter Solstice 384YE.

384YE Summer Solstice winds of fortune.d: Six eternals answered the archmages' plenipotentiary messages, and the Summer tourney for the Icy Crag reached its climax. Imperial fleets and units smuggled trapped citizens out of Feroz, infuriating Governor Rahab. Moonwater Hall's abrogation led to fires and a Faraden coup. An unnatural drought gripped the Empire while Syrene's Wisdom flooded with Winter-tainted water. Dawn pressed into the Barrens, the Zenith crusade continued, and the Skallahn raid yielded only loot. Elsewhere, Bounder's Hall opened in Sarcombe, Isaella's Dance was raised in Miaren, the magistrates crushed the Yaw'nagrah cults, and both thresher mandates took effect. Opportunities arose in Therunin, Redoubt, the Sarangrave and Tsark.

n.Dawn: Dawnish armies led the invasion of the Barrens from north and south after Dawn challenged the Imperial Orcs to a glorious contest, though the General Assembly was displeased; Glory Square also hosted the Summer tourney melee.
n.Druj: The Druj faced pressure on several fronts: an appraisal into stirring an uprising in the Sarangrave, the continuing Highborn crusade in Zenith, and Dawn cutting the Barrens in two.
n.Grendel: Governor Rahab was furious after Imperial forces smuggled citizens out of Feroz, while a Grendel Paymaster planned an audacious raid on Tsark and sanctions continued to penalise Imperial trade with Oran.
n.Highguard: The Citadel Guard and the Highborn crusade drove the Zenith invasion forward, while a Winter-tainted flood devastated Syrene's Wisdom in Casinea.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' ambition to claim the Barrens drew a challenge from Dawn, whose armies then moved quickly to seize the advantage there.
n.Jotun: The Imperial raid into Skallahn did little to harm the Jotun war effort, but the Empire could exploit what it learned with a second raid; meanwhile Imperial units lay in wait at Hotter's Mire in Jotun-held Liathaven.
n.Navarr: Navarr gained a third army, Isaella's Dance, in Miaren, while Therunin's brokers put forward new opportunities and Navarr were drawn into the Heirs of Terunael affair at Hotter's Mire and talks with visitors about Terunael relics.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn trapped in Feroz were successfully evacuated, Marracossan refugees took up residence in Madruga, and magistrates pursued smugglers operating across Segura and Kahraman.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Tassato priests and Rezia di Tassato are tagged in the Faraden developments, and Tassato is named as wealthy trading gateway near Sarcombe.
n.The Marches: The Marcher thresher mandate took effect, a Bounder's Hall opened in Sarcombe to protect Mournwold orcs, and the abrogation of Moonwater Hall in Upwold spiralled into fires and a Faraden coup.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov is among those tagged in connection with the drought and the Spring conjunction.
n.Urizen: The Urizen National Assembly warned of dire repercussions should the liberation of Zenith be left unfinished, the Shrine of the Armsmaster in Redoubt sparked new opportunities, and several rituals were added to Urizen lore.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Varushkan Assembly is tagged regarding the Barrens, and the liberation of Ossium is cited when comparing the Druj miasma.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark Assembly's concerns about building a fane prompted a proposal for a Conclave title to oversee them, while Winterfolk worried about their skeins after actions in Sermersuaq were coming to Anvil.

t.Astolat: The Free Folk refugees from Arracossa lived in Astolat as guests of the House of the Proffered Hand, with their own ambitions and problems for their neighbours.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the trade winds included a demand from the Steward of Bregasland, with Bregas Marchers especially tagged.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the defeat of the Heirs of Terunael in Brocéliande is credited with helping the magistrates break the Yaw'nagrah cults.
t.Casinea: A devastating flood infused with Winter magic burst from the Syrene's Wisdom mine and swept through the town of Syrene, threatening the Bourse seat.
t.Feroz: Imperial fleets and military units secretly smuggled trapped citizens out of Grendel-held Feroz, leaving Governor Rahab furious.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the defence of Hercynia is credited with helping make the magistrates' campaign against Yaw'nagrah a success.
t.Kahraman: Magistrates were investigating Faraden and Imperial smugglers evading Senate tariffs across Kahraman's borders, and Kahraman is noted as overlooked by Sarcombe.
t.Liathaven: Elite Imperial units surrounded the Feni settlement of Hotter's Mire to stop the Heirs of Terunael breaking the territory's Winter curse, and Liathaven now holds a relatively stable, openly-living Feni population.
t.Madruga: The Marracossan refugees settled in the abandoned town of Trajadoz, showing little interest in integrating with their Imperial neighbours.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel Paymaster planning the Tsark raid belonged to the North Mareave Trading Consortium.
t.Miaren: The third Navarr army, Isaella's Dance, completed its muster in Miaren and awaited its first general.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Meade is named as the northern trading centre Sarcombe could one day rival.
t.Mountains of the Moon: A Grendel Paymaster proposed a surprise raid over the peaks to seize Tsark's mithril and white granite, inviting Imperial citizens to join while others vowed to oppose it.
t.Mournwold: Bounder's Hall was completed in Sarcombe to protect the pacifist Mournwold orcs, renewing interest in the territory's prosperity, while Mournwold Marchers accepted their Assembly's lawful approach to sorcerers.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the miasma of the Sarangrave is compared to that faced during the liberation of Ossium.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov is tagged in the wind on the drought and Spring conjunction.
t.Redoubt: The newly consecrated Shrine of the Armsmaster on Mount Siluri became a place of pilgrimage and inspired new opportunities, and Redoubt's Grand Harbour is cited as a fruit of the Cardinal of Prosperity's attention.
t.Sarangrave: An appraisal examined how the Imperial spy network might inspire an uprising against the three Druj clans dominating these miasma-choked marshes.
t.Segura: Magistrates were investigating Faraden and Imperial smugglers operating across Segura's borders, armed with a list of suspects recovered from a rescued magistrate.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Winterfolk visiting Anvil are concerned about their skeins following their dubious actions in Sermersuaq.
t.Skallahn: The Imperial raid into Skallahn gained only some loot, but yielded insight that could support a swift second attack before the Jarls shore up their defences.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Urizen, especially those in Spiral, are tagged in the trade winds roundup.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato priests are tagged in the Faraden developments, and the city is named as the wealthy gateway linked to Sarcombe.
t.The Barrens: Dawnish armies drove into the Barrens from north and south, cutting the territory in two amid their contest with the Imperial Orcs, to the displeasure of the General Assembly.
t.Therunin: Therunin's brokers proposed Thornsong House, a major expansion of the Feverwater dredging, and an offer of help from the orcs of the Great Forest to enrich the territory.
t.Upwold: After the Senate abrogated Moonwater Hall, events in Upwold spiralled into fires, accusations and a Faraden coup.
t.Zenith: The Imperial invasion led by the Citadel Guard and the Highborn crusade made progress, aided by the Loyalty assembly, while Urizen warned of repercussions if the liberation is left unfinished.

r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Mentioned in passing: the defeat of the Heirs of Terunael in Brocéliande is credited in the Yaw'nagrah investigation, though the region is not named.
r.Feroz/Afarjasse: The grace period for Afarjasse's people to leave Feroz ended at the Spring Equinox, before the covert evacuation of the remaining citizens.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Citizens trapped in the Cazar Straits, given no grace period to leave, were smuggled out under cover of darkness by Imperial fleets and units.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Citizens trapped in Fontargenta, denied any grace period, were successfully spirited away in the stealthy Imperial evacuation.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The grace period for Morajasse's people to leave Feroz ended at the Spring Equinox, before the covert evacuation of those trapped elsewhere.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Citizens trapped in Oranseri, given no chance to leave legally, were smuggled out from under the Grendel Governor's nose.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Clearing Alderly to remove an outlaw haven and open up farmland and hardwoods has been discussed for at least a year as a way to boost the Mournwold's prosperity.

384YE Summer Solstice winds of war.d: The Lasambrian Jotun, aided by their Mournwold allies, claimed Gambit and later Jade Range. An enchantment and the delay at Rotoga kept them from raiding the Great Mine of Briante and the Damatian Cliffs. Mathilda Fisher pressed her claim to Bregasland with Jotun support, and the Empire ceded Grey Fens and the Ottermire. Imperial and Otkodov forces drove the Jotun from Suaq Fount and Suaq Wastes, leaving Sermersuaq for the Senate to assign. Druj from Ulnak destroyed the Tower of the Scorpion in Echofell. The Empire struck the Carmine Fields and Hope's Rest in a pincer. In Zenith the Druj held the Imperial advance at Clypion. Four battle opportunities and many conjunctions were identified.

n.Dawn: Dawnish armies could not take the Cautious Advance or Give Ground orders, and a horror from the Spring realm threatened them in the Barrens. In Semmerholm the Adamant Gate could not fall below 1,000 strength, and Barien offered an audience to those who completed his Challenge.
n.Druj: The Druj retook Echofell in Ossium and attacked hard in Zenith, holding the Imperial advance. However, they could not stop the Empire carving a Steel Causeway through the Barrens despite the rebuilt Spires of the Dusk.
n.Highguard: Highborn armies gained double natural resupply and could issue the Crusading Storm order. They also received bonuses when attacking into Zenith from Morrow or defending Morrow against attacks from Zenith.
n.Imperial Orcs: A conjunction in Bregasland gave the Imperial Orcs an opportunity to recover the artefact Pilgrim's Shield Oath-Heart.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun took Gambit and Jade Range in Kahraman and backed Mathilda Fisher's seizure of Bregasland, but they were driven from Suaq Fount and Suaq Wastes and held only the forts of Tanikipari and Stark.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a conjunction in Karsk offered a chance to rescue kidnapped Navarr and recover an ancient relic.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast lost Gambit and Jade Range in Kahraman to the Jotun, though the Great Mine of Briante and the Damatian Cliffs were protected from raids. Wave Riders raided Segura.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Temeschwar was suggested to lead a mission to recover a Bloodwater Spear orc from the Druj.
n.The Marches: Bregasland was lost to the Jotun-backed Mathilda Fisher, and former Mournwold warriors fought for the Jotun. Marcher armies could not take Give Ground, but any Imperial army could billet in Bregasland, Upwold or Mitwold.
n.Thule: Otkodov allied with the Empire to liberate Sermersuaq, and the Thule garrison of Fljajokep aided Echofell's defenders. A Thule warlock captured by the Jotun awaited rescue.
n.Urizen: Urizen's former territory of Zenith saw a bitter, stalled struggle, and a battle opportunity aimed to inspire Urizen to engage in Iteri. The Citadel Guard would begin to deteriorate again after the Solstice.
n.Varushka: Varushka lost Echofell in Ossium to the Druj, and three conjunctions in Karsk dealt with the self-styled Boyar of Isember and his dark power. Varushkan armies would suffer reduced victory points when campaigning alongside Brass Coast or Wintermark armies.
n.Wintermark: Sermersuaq was liberated from the Jotun, ghosts haunted Bruckland in Hahnmark, and Wintermark armies gained the Fight with Honour order along with modified effects against the Jotun.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland was ceded to Mathilda Fisher and her Jotun allies and was no longer Imperial. Conjunctions there concerned Oath-Heart and House Greywater's escape, and Imperial armies could still billet there.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: the Druj invasion of Ossium came out of the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Hahnmark: A conjunction at Turelva in Bruckland sought to help haunting ghostly spirits pass on.
t.Kahraman: The Lasambrian Jotun claimed Gambit and then Jade Range, though raids on the Great Mine of Briante and the Damatian Cliffs were prevented. A battle opportunity aimed to stymie Lasambrian efforts to isolate fortifications.
t.Karsk: Three conjunctions in Lestazny addressed the self-styled Boyar of Isember, his dark power, and kidnapped Navarr with an ancient relic.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: any Imperial army could take the Billet order in Mitwold.
t.Morrow: Highborn or Urizen armies attacking into Zenith from Morrow, or defending Morrow against attacks from Zenith, gained territory bonuses but inflicted fewer casualties.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: warriors formerly of Mournwold fought as allies of the Jotun and were expected opponents in the Kahraman battle.
t.Ossium: The Druj invaded, destroyed the Tower of the Scorpion and retook the forests of Echofell, and a conjunction sought to stop them destroying the Bone Hives.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the alliance of Empire and Otkodov drove the Jotun from much of Sermersuaq.
t.Sarangrave: A conjunction in Bloodwater Marsh sought to recover a Bloodwater Spear orc from the Druj, and the ghulai of Sarangrave sought a magical text in Zenith.
t.Segura: A conjunction at Cereva Hall in Lucksprings offered the chance to intercept a raiding party of Wave Riders on Imperial soil.
t.Semmerholm: The Adamant Gate could not be reduced below 1,000 military strength, and Barien held a grand audience at the Semmerstones for those who completed his Challenge.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq became Imperial again after Suaq Fount and Suaq Wastes were freed, though the Jotun held Tanikipari and Stark. The Senate had to assign it to a nation and allocate the Pride of Ikka's Tears.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Temeschwar was named as responsible for a conjunction in Sarangrave.
t.The Barrens: After three years the Empire attacked again, carving a Steel Causeway through the heart of the Barrens with barely a casualty. A battle opportunity and several conjunctions aimed to secure the Imperial presence.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: any Imperial army could take the Billet order in Upwold.
t.Zenith: Two massive forces clashed, and the Druj went on the attack but failed to drive out the Empire, though they halted its advance. A battle opportunity aimed to claim a beachhead in Clypion.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The Empire was forced to cede Grey Fens to the Jotun-backed forces.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The Ottermire was ceded after Grey Fens, and a conjunction at Greywater Estate offered to help House Greywater escape a Jotun execution squad.
r.Hahnmark/Bruckland: A conjunction at Turelva sought to help the ghostly spirits haunting the area pass on.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Lasambrian Jotun claimed the plains of Gambit despite the efforts of Imperial heroes.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The defenders of Fort Braydon could not match the orcs' zeal, and the Jotun took control of Jade Range shortly before the Solstice.
r.Ossium/Echofell: The Druj destroyed the Tower of the Scorpion and retook Echofell's forests, and a conjunction aimed to stop them destroying the Bone Hives.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: A conjunction at Dead Stone Woods sought to recover a Bloodwater Spear orc from the Druj.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: A conjunction at Cereva Hall offered the chance to intercept a raiding party of Wave Riders.
r.Semmerholm/Causse: A grand audience with Barien at the Semmerstones offered rewards to those who completed his Challenge.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The Imperial advance faltered at Stark's forts. Conjunctions there sought to free a hylje hostage at White Plume Rocks and retrieve a captured Thule warlock at Flat Hills.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The Empire and Otkodov drove the Jotun out of Suaq Fount.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The Jotun were driven from Suaq Wastes, and a conjunction at Spirax wood sought to deny them the Spear of Bounty.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: The forts of Tanikipari halted the allied advance and remained a Jotun stronghold.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: A conjunction at Saltmaw offered the chance to unleash the Barren Sea to flood the Fangs and the Saltmarsh.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Imperial armies attacked the southern hills of Hope's Rest as one arm of the pincer to cut the Barrens in half.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: The Saltmarsh was a target of a proposed opportunity to flood it with the Barren Sea from Saltmaw.
r.The Barrens/The Carmine Fields: Imperial armies attacked the northern Carmine Fields as part of the pincer, and a conjunction at the Red Plains sought to retrieve cursed treasure threatening the Wolves of War.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Orc and Imperial forces were locked in a bitter struggle for its hills. A battle opportunity aimed to claim a beachhead there, and conjunctions dealt with a malaise and with ex-prisoners in its groves.
r.Zenith/Iteri: A battle opportunity sought to inspire Urizen to engage in Iteri.
r.Zenith/Lustri: A conjunction at Sleetstorm Pass sought to deny the ghulai of Sarangrave a mysterious magical text.
r.Zenith/Proceris: A conjunction at the Golden Cascade sought to recover the Amulet of Truth from a wicked Druj warleader.

Abrogate Moonwater Hall.d: Moonwater Hall had been commissioned in Summer 381YE and built with the help of the Faraden merchant families. It provided the benefits of a great work in Upwold, adding income to the territory's farms and businesses. The Senate voted to abrogate it, and the motion passed. Most of the buildings were pulled down, and the Faraden were informed that the Senate no longer wished them to congregate there. The Faraden reacted with some anger. They asked for, and were granted, a week to put their affairs in order, make preparations and send messengers to Faraden merchants visiting the Empire. The hall no longer provides any benefit to Upwold.

n.The Marches: Marcher farms and businesses in Upwold lost the extra income Moonwater Hall had provided, and the Faraden merchant presence in their land was dismissed.

t.Upwold: Moonwater Hall was largely torn down, ending its trade benefits to Upwold's farms and businesses, and the Faraden were given a week to leave.

All in red.d: After Moonwater Hall in Upwold was abrogated and torn down, the Court of Five Winds asked for recompense for the 20 wains of white granite and 20 crowns Faraden families had invested. Six weeks later Modnos agents set fires in Tassato and Redoubt. There were no deaths. Five arsonists were arrested, refused to pay their fines and face likely execution, and Chief Magistrate Stanislav Karkovich was asked for advice. The Modnos lifted their bounties on Livia and Astrid but raised the bounty on Colwynn de Rondell to 30 Thrones. Tchinua Ganbatar then deposed the Lady of the Five Winds, and an envoy is promised for the Autumn Equinox to discuss the Liberty Pact, sanctions and religious attitudes.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Imperial help to Faraden against the Jotun is cited as one reason some Faraden families value the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Tsagaan grudge over the execution of the Brass Coast's Honradez sisters is noted, and the new Faraden ambassador has arrived at the embassy in Segura.
n.The League: Tassato's Blood Red River Museum was badly burned and three arsonists were held there. The Senate may now repair or grandly expand the museum, the printing houses of Tassato and Sarvos could take over publishing Echoes of the Labyrinth, and League ambassador Erasmo di Tassato faces a delicate diplomatic task. Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato is no longer under a Modnos bounty.
n.The Marches: Moonwater Hall in Upwold was closed and torn down by Marcher militia and magistrates. It no longer benefits Marcher farms and businesses, and the Faraden want payment for their lost investment.
n.Urizen: Spider's Vantage Spire was nearly gutted, losing its printing press and warehouses. Its torchbearers plan to rebuild themselves, which halts widespread publication of Echoes of the Labyrinth for about six months. Livia of the Celestial Cascade is no longer under a Modnos bounty.

t.Redoubt: Modnos arsonists nearly gutted Spider's Vantage Spire, destroying its printing press and warehouses. Two Faraden were arrested and face likely execution.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: its printing houses are named as a possible alternative publisher of Echoes of the Labyrinth if the Senate amends its motion.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden embassy is in Segura, where the new ambassador Arban Tuvalk arrived with letters from the new Liege.
t.Tassato: The Blood Red River Museum was gutted in one wing and many artworks were lost, so its Pride congregation benefits are suspended. The Senate can repair it or rebuild it on a grander scale before the Autumn Equinox 384YE, or lose the site.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the damaged museum was paid for by Temeschwar's Bloody Butchers Guild and built on foundations laid by Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar.
t.Upwold: Moonwater Hall was abrogated and most of its buildings demolished, ending its benefits to Upwold's farms and businesses and sending Faraden merchants away aggrieved.

Begin to speak.d: Azoth declined a parley but sent its servants to hold another night market in the Hall of Worlds on Friday night. Jaheris invited the Archmage of Summer to a parley in the grove of sighs and asked for representatives of House de Rondell. Roshanwe accepted the Archmage of Day's parley with a set guest list. Estavus declined a parley but, with the City of Gold and Lead, offered mystic scrolls for four war rituals and some warm ashes in exchange for Ephisis' Scales bargains. Tharim agreed to parley with the Archmage of Winter. Siakha demanded that the Empire, bearing the Staff of Spring, take the Stone of Storms from her Druj favoured in the Stormwood before she would send any message. Her herald then attacked citizens in Anvil.

n.Dawn: Jaheris specifically asked for representatives of House de Rondell of Dawn to attend his parley in the grove of sighs. The Archmage of Spring, Ser Fabienne De Miel, faces Siakha's challenge to bring the Staff of Spring to the Stormwood.
n.Druj: A band of Druj favoured by Siakha holds the Stone of Storms in the Stormwood, possibly supported by Siakhan heralds. The Empire is expected to fight them to the death to claim it.
n.Urizen: Two Urizen archmages were involved. Elyssiathain, Archmage of Night, was refused a parley by Azoth but offered a night market, while Ematius, Archmage of Winter, secured a parley with Tharim.

t.The Barrens: A conjunction through the Sentinel Gate offered the Empire a way into the Druj-held Barrens to face Siakha's favoured and take the Stone of Storms.

r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Stormwood in the Bleaks was named as the place where Siakha's Druj favoured await the Spring Archmage's force with the Stone of Storms. The conjunction was set for five o'clock on the Saturday.

Build up my body.d: Sophus of the Guiding Lights proposed expanding the Academy of Arms in Siluri with a gymnasium, palaestra, accommodation and auditorium, costing 25 wains of white granite and 50 crowns over three months. It would create the Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine (10 liao, 20 Synod votes, appointed annually by the Assembly of Ambition) and let one starting military unit train there each season for a free upgrade. The Circle of the Shimmering Forge invited citizens to donate materials to Provost Lord Florette Griffinsbane so artisans could craft up to five magic items each season for Anvil's Academy students. The Senate could also commission Academy great works in Astolat, Hercynia, Holberg and Sarvos, each giving 30 Synod votes and 15 liao. The pilgrimage opportunities last until the end of the Spring Equinox 385YE.

n.Dawn: A Dawnish priest, Ranae de Rondell, raised the consecration mandate that sparked this interest, and House de Kucant is among the artisans offering to craft items for Anvil's Academy; Dawn's Astolat Academy could also be expanded as a great work.
n.Navarr: The Steading of Evergreen Tears joined the artisans supporting Anvil's Academy, and Navarr-held Hercynia hosts one of the four Academies the Senate could expand into a great work.
n.The League: The League holds two of the four territories, Holberg and Sarvos, whose Academies of Arms could be expanded into great works for Ambition's congregations, and the Guild of Good Grapes joined the artisans supporting Anvil's Academy.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Academy of Arms in Redoubt, Adelmar's own and now consecrated, drew rising pilgrim numbers and could be expanded into a grand pilgrimage site with a new Synod title, while the Citadel of Shining Quartz joined the artisans aiding Anvil's Academy.

t.Astolat: The Academy of Arms in Astolat could be expanded by Senate commission into a great work providing 30 Synod votes and 15 liao to its congregations of Ambition.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia's Academy of Arms is one of four large enough to be expanded into a great work granting 30 Synod votes and 15 liao to Ambition congregations there.
t.Holberg: Holberg's Academy of Arms could be enlarged into a great work to house pilgrims, providing 30 Synod votes and 15 liao for its congregations of Ambition.
t.Redoubt: The newly consecrated Academy of Arms in Redoubt saw growing crowds of pilgrims and could be expanded into a major place of pilgrimage with its own Synod title.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's Academy of Arms could be expanded by Senate commission into a great work providing 30 Synod votes and 15 liao to local congregations of Ambition.

r.Redoubt/Siluri: Reached by a treacherous mountain path, the Siluri Academy of Arms could gain a gymnasium, palaestra, pilgrim lodgings and auditorium, creating the Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine and letting one starting military unit train there each season for an upgrade.

Construct Angelica Memorial House of Hea.d: The motion called for a self-funded sinecure in Riposi, a garden of tailored and peaceful grounds intended to heal the malign and mental maladies of war and to grow herbs for producing cerulean mazzarine, specifically for the use of the League national block. Its custodian is to hold the Imperial title of Mistress of Medicine, a tenured position appointed by the generals of the League. No costs were specified, so the civil service assumed the minimum size of 10 wains. Shauni di Vergo provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood after the Summer Solstice 384YE. Once completed, the sinecure will create the title.

n.The League: The League gains a herb garden whose produce is reserved for its national block, together with a new title, the Mistress of Medicine, to be appointed by the League's generals.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos is to host the memorial house of healing, which honours Angelica Vergo di Sarvos and was proposed by the territory's own senator.

r.Sarvos/Riposi: Riposi is the site chosen for the sinecure's healing gardens. These will grow herbs for cerulean mazzarine and tend to those suffering the maladies of war.

Construct Bladeroot Sinecure.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, the motion commissioned a sinecure for the production of bladeroot, to be built in Old Ranging. The motion called it self funded and did not define its costs, so the civil service assumed the minimum size of 10 wains, with standard costs applying. After the Summer Solstice 384YE, Radic Splinterovich Schaslyvyy provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood. Once completed, the sinecure will create the Imperial title of Steward of the Nabarr, appointed by the senators of Navarr.

n.Navarr: Navarr's senators will appoint the new Steward of the Nabarr once the sinecure is completed, giving the nation control of a bladeroot-producing Imperial title within its own lands.

t.Hercynia: Hercynia's senator proposed the motion, and the territory will be home to the new bladeroot herb garden sinecure once construction is completed.

r.Hercynia/Old Ranging: Old Ranging is the chosen site for the bladeroot sinecure, with materials and money already supplied towards its construction after the Summer Solstice.

Construct Crimson Drummers of Madruga.d: The commission was announced in Summer 384YE by Ahraz i Guerra under his Imperial Wayleave rather than passed by a Senate vote. It was to be built in Torres in Madruga at a cost of 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns in labour, taking three months, with Ahraz funding it in full. After the Summer Solstice he provided 3 thrones and 12 wains of white granite. Once complete, the sinecure would create a new Imperial title, the Crimson Sutannir, with tenure, appointed by judgement of the Brass Coast National Assembly and providing liao and Synod votes.

n.The Brass Coast: A Freeborn citizen funded a new sinecure whose title, the Crimson Sutannir, would be chosen by the Brass Coast National Assembly, giving the Freeborn a tenured position supplying liao and Synod votes.

t.Madruga: The Crimson Drummers of Madruga were commissioned to be built in this Brass Coast territory, with materials for the work provided after the Summer Solstice.

r.Madruga/Torres: Torres was named as the site of the new sinecure, a three-month build of white granite paid for entirely by Ahraz i Guerra.

Construct Garden of Imperial Auxiliaries.d: Proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by Holberg, the motion commissioned a herb garden sinecure in Coursmouth. Once completed it creates the Imperial title of Legate of the Imperial Auxiliaries, elected by the Military Council and able to address it. The Legate is responsible for supporting the Imperial Auxiliaries in helping the Field Marshal communicate on major conjunctions through the sentinel gate, and is revocable by the General and the Assembly of Nine. As no size was specified, the civil service assumed the minimum of 10 wains. Ray Fosterbrooke provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood after the Summer Solstice.

n.Highguard: Highguard's Necropolis gains a new Imperial sinecure on its soil, with Highguard's Necropolis senator having proposed the motion.

t.Necropolis: Necropolis's senator proposed the motion, and the garden is to be built within the territory to support the Imperial Auxiliaries' work at the sentinel gate.

r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Coursmouth is the site of the Garden of the Imperial Auxiliaries, a herb garden sinecure whose completion creates the title of Legate of the Imperial Auxiliaries.

Construct Greenwood Manor.d: The commission was announced by Bertrand under an Imperial Wayleave rather than raised in the usual way. It cost 10 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood and 40 crowns in labour, and would take three months to build. After the Summer Solstice Bertrand supplied 5 thrones, 10 wains of weirwood and 10 wains of white granite. Once complete, the commission would create two Imperial titles, the Knight of the Greenwood and the Reeve of the Greenwood Fair. Both would be elected annually by the Dawnish National Assembly and could be revoked by the General Assembly or the Dawnish National Assembly.

n.Dawn: Once the manor is complete, the Dawnish National Assembly gains the power to elect, and to revoke, the new Knight of the Greenwood and Reeve of the Greenwood Fair each year.

t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm is to gain Greenwood Manor and a renovated Greenwood Market, funded with materials and money provided by Bertrand after the Summer Solstice.

r.Semmerholm/Elvette: Elvette is the site of the commission, where Greenwood Manor was to be built and the Greenwood Market renovated over three months.

Construct Highwatch Citadel.d: The commission followed a Wind of Fortune offer from a herald of Zakalwe. The offer had expired the previous season, but after the Conclave thanked Zakalwe and voted to accept it, a one-season extension was granted. The work cost 20 wains of white granite, 40 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Summer Solstice Ka'bal provided five thrones and five wains of granite, and fifteen other contributors gave one wain each. Once complete, the expansion would create a new Imperial title, the Polemarch of Highwatch, appointed annually by Urizen's senators. The announcement said it would provide vis and pearls to enchant an army attacking the Druj.

n.Druj: The expanded citadel was promised to supply vis and pearls to enchant an Imperial army attacking the Druj.
n.Urizen: Urizen's senators would gain the power to appoint a new Polemarch of Highwatch each year once the citadel expansion in their territory of Morrow was complete.

t.Morrow: Highwatch Citadel in Urizen-held Morrow was to be expanded to house heralds of Zakalwe. The work needed 20 wains of white granite, all of which were provided after the Summer Solstice.

r.Morrow/Altis: Altis is the site of Highwatch Citadel, where three months of construction were commissioned to add rooms for Zakalwe's heralds.

Construct Mudlark's Haven.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Hercynia. It took up a limited opportunity, described as fully funded, to build a fortified steading called "Mudlark's Haven" as an expansion of the Feverwater Docks. The cost was 6 wains of white granite, 12 wains of weirwood and 36 crowns in labour, with three months to construct. After the Summer Solstice, Travid Longest Path provided 4 thrones 4 crowns along with all of the weirwood and granite. Once complete, the Dredgemaster of Feverwater gains a larger seasonal income of ingots and access to a ministry. The expanded docks also let Navarr military units take the Adventure in the Sarangrave action.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-held Sarangrave is named as the target of a new Adventure in the Sarangrave action open to Navarr armies once the docks are expanded.
n.Navarr: Navarr gained an expanded Feverwater Docks in its territory of Therunin, funded by Travid Longest Path. Once complete, Navarr military units can take the Adventure in the Sarangrave action.

t.Sarangrave: The expanded docks give Navarr military units a new route into the Druj-held Sarangrave through the Adventure in the Sarangrave action.
t.Therunin: The fortified steading of Mudlark's Haven was commissioned in the Feverwater. Once complete it expands the Feverwater Docks and raises the Dredgemaster's ingot income, as well as giving access to a ministry.

Construct Ratibor's Gate Shrine.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Casinea, the motion commissioned the rededication of Ratibor's Gate as an inspirational memorial to the exemplar Ratibor of Temeschwar. The work cost 20 wains of white granite, 5 thrones (40 crowns in labour) and a dose of true liao, and took three months to construct. Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided the granite and money after the Summer Solstice, and Laughlan of the Crimson Reaper Cartel supplied the true liao. Once completed it created an inspirational tomb and the Imperial title of Watcher of Ratibor's Torch, appointed by the League National Assembly.

n.The League: The League gained an inspirational memorial to one of its exemplars, funded by League citizens, and its National Assembly gained the right to appoint the new Watcher of Ratibor's Torch.

t.Temeschwar: Ratibor's Gate in Temeschwar was rededicated and built up as an inspirational tomb to Ratibor of Temeschwar, a project put forward by the territory's own senator.

Construct Statue of Eleonaris.d: Announced by Sagua i'Ezmara, Master of the Koboldi, at the Conclave's urgent request, the statue honours victories in Semmerholm, Ossium and the wider Empire achieved alongside the Knights of Glory, and the long relationship with Eleonaris. It cost 30 wains of white granite, 60 crowns in labour and three months to build. Gancio di Catazar provided 7 thrones, 4 crowns and the 30 wains of white granite after the Summer Solstice. While Sagua installed the Runic Hearth of Adamant, Amica Peddler, proxy senator of Semmerholm, took over the Koboldi's hospitality duties. The Imperial Senate ceded control of the statue in the same session, and the Queen of the Fields of Glory laid claim to it in the town of Semmer's Rose.

n.Dawn: The statue stands in Dawnish Semmerholm and honours Dawn's long relationship with Eleonaris and the Knights of Glory, and Semmerholm's proxy senator Amica Peddler took on the Koboldi's Dawnish hospitality.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the statue celebrates victories in Ossium, a Varushkan-held territory, among others.

t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: victories in Ossium are among those the statue celebrates.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm gains a statue of Eleonaris at its end of the Golden Causeway, commemorating victories won there, though the Queen of the Fields of Glory has claimed it after the Senate ceded control.

r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: The statue is built in Lacuve beside the Golden Causeway, and the Queen of the Fields of Glory has claimed the monument in the town of Semmer's Rose.

Construct White Roads.d: Proposed by Casinea and seconded by Sarvos, the motion called for a single commission based on earlier designs by Johanna of Ravensfell and was described as self-funded. The cost, as set out in the related Wind of Fortune, was 120 wains of white granite and 240 crowns in labour, with six months needed for construction. Rhesa supplied 15 thrones and 60 wains of white granite after the Summer Solstice 384YE, and the same again after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the White Roads will act as great works raising the income of farms and businesses in all three territories.

n.Highguard: All three territories to be linked by the White Roads are Highborn lands, so the Highborn stand to gain greater prosperity for their farms and businesses, along with more pilgrims at the hostels of Virtue's Rest.

t.Bastion: Bastion is one of the three territories where the White Roads are to be built, raising the income of its farms and businesses once construction is finished.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis will receive a stretch of the White Roads, which will boost the income of its farms and businesses once the six months of construction are complete.
t.Reikos: Reikos is included in the White Roads commission, and its farms and businesses will earn more once the great work is complete.

Construct Zemress Naval Academy.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Tassato, the motion commissioned the academy at a cost of 10 wains of white granite, 15 of weirwood, 10 of mithril and 70 crowns in labour, taking six months to build, with 5 thrones in seasonal upkeep. After the Summer Solstice, Esteban I Del Rio Blanco I Guerra provided the mithril, weirwood, white granite and 8 thrones 6 crowns. Once complete, researchers would present three possible qualities for new Imperial navies, and the fleet owners of the Brass Coast would vote on which mattered most; the winning quality would become the focus of a year's research.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast gained a naval academy on its soil, built with materials and coin supplied by Esteban I Del Rio Blanco I Guerra, and its fleet owners were given the vote on which quality the school's research into new Imperial navies would pursue.

t.Madruga: Madruga became the site of the Zemress Naval Academy, a six-month construction that would host Imperial students studying and researching naval warfare.

Deep when the river's high.d: About twenty thousand Imperial troops (the Tusks, Strong Reeds, Bounders and Winter Sun) faced roughly thirty thousand Jotun alongside Mathilda Fisher's Yegarra. A cautious Imperial advance into Grey Fens was overwhelmed and pushed back into Ottermire. Despite Night magic, flooded fields and barricades, the Jotun stormed Ottery's western gates and the Imperials retreated south to Sallow in the Rushes. Nearly fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers and well over a thousand Jotun fell. Bregasland became a Jotun territory and Fisher declared herself Steward of Bregasland, though most Bregas rejected her. Imperial heroes could save the Greywaters from Ulfur executioners, and the Imperial Orcs could try to take Oath-Heart from Dillion Fisher.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun force-marched from Segura to bolster the Marchers but shared in the defeat and retreat to Sallow. Sinokenon named the Imperial Orcs as exemplars of Loyalty and offered them, through Archmage of Day Gralka, the chance to recover Oath-Heart from Dillion Fisher.
n.Jotun: Jotun armies led by the Mandowla's Roar overwhelmed the Imperials in Grey Fens and Ottermire, stormed Ottery and conquered Bregasland, though they lost well over a thousand warriors. They are now offering the Bregas the Choice in the name of their puppet Steward, Mathilda Fisher.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun's general said their Brass Coast allies must rest as the orcs left Segura to march north.
n.The Marches: The Marches lost Bregasland to the Jotun after the Tusks, Strong Reeds and Bounders were driven out of Grey Fens and Ottermire, leaving many Bregas as thralls, in hiding or as refugees. Some households have sided with Mathilda Fisher, while House Greywater plans to resist.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not directly named in this account of the Bregasland fighting.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland fell to the Jotun when Ottermire was lost, and Mathilda Fisher proclaimed herself its Steward. The Rushes and Gravenmarch remain in Imperial hands and a sizeable Marcher population stays on under occupation.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun broke Ottery's gates with a rune-carved tree trunk apparently carried all the way from Hordalant.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: retreating east to Odd's End and the safety of Mitwold was considered, but the Imperial forces went south instead.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not directly named in this account.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun made its long, enchanted march north from Segura to join the fighting in Bregasland.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold wood shipped along the Otterway was used to build barricades and spikes around Ottery.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Gravenmarch stays in Imperial hands, and many displaced Bregas have moved there and been grudgingly taken in.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The first clash took place among the dead pools of Grey Fens, where the Imperial advance stalled and was driven out. If House Greywater escapes there to wage a guerrilla campaign, Grey Fens will hold allied insurgents working for the Empire.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: The Jotun assault struck south out of North Fens, and a few smaller households there have thrown in their lot with Mathilda Fisher.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Ottermire saw the decisive Battle of Ottery, where the Jotun smashed the western gates and took the region, turning its protective mists against the Empire. A conjunction to the Greywater estate there offers a chance to stop the Ulfur sent to execute the household.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: The beaten Imperial armies retreated past Sabbey's Mound to Sallow in the Rushes, which remains Imperial and has taken in Bregas refugees.

Delirium.d: Nearly seventy units, mostly Dawnish and Varushkan, backed by the Varushkan Assembly, Karsk's magistrates and the Ketsov, stormed Isember. Slain outlaws rose as husks under a plaguewulf's curse, so the Sovereign's Heart and its tunnels were burned. The boyar Alexi Iskandrova Isembrioch and the creature remain unaccounted for, but trade along the Iron Roads now flows freely. In Ossium, twenty thousand Druj, including the Black Wind, overwhelmed the Tower of the Scorpion despite Thule help, took the Echofell and were repulsed from the Drownbark Forest. Conjunctions offered chances to defend the Bone Hives, hunt the boyar, confront the horror in the Whispering Glade and rescue captured Navarri.

n.Dawn: Dawnish knights and yeofolk made up most of the forces that destroyed Isember, some sailing in to Ivarsgard, while Dawnish knights helped defend the Tower of the Scorpion and Dawnish prisoners were shot down by the Black Wind.
n.Druj: A Druj host of twenty thousand, including the burning-beetle army, the scorpion banners and the Black Wind, built siege engines, destroyed the Tower of the Scorpion and conquered the Echofell, but failed to break into the Drownbark Forest.
n.Navarr: A Navarr was the first to notice the sickness among the Isember bandits, and two Sunstalker thorns carrying a relic of ancient Emrys were held captive, prompting a rescue opportunity for the Dean of the First Voice Glade.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: scoundrels from Temeschwar were among the outlaws who joined the Isember bandits.
n.Thule: Thule warriors from Flajokep helped defend the Tower of the Scorpion and lost half their number when it fell, then withdrew to the Bonewood, refusing to return unless Imperial armies defend Ossium.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Druj tactic of destroying hives had already been used ruthlessly in Zenith and elsewhere in Urizen.
n.Varushka: Varushkan warbands, wardens and the Assembly ended the Isember bandit threat, leaving few outlaws in the nation, but Varushkan vales in Ossium suffered heavily as the Druj took the Echofell and the Tower of the Scorpion.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: the Druj invasion force emerged from the Forest of Ulnak into the Echofell.
t.Karsk: Isember was destroyed and its outlaws killed or tried, making trade and travel along Karsk's Iron Roads much easier, though the robber-boyar and the plaguewulf remain at large near the ruins.
t.Ossium: The Druj returned in force, destroying the Tower of the Scorpion and seizing the Echofell, while panic spread among the new vales; the clearing of Karsk did, however, open supply routes for Ossium's settlement.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: some of the Isember bandits were scoundrels from as far afield as Temeschwar.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: some Dawnish forces crossed the Semmerlak by ship to land at Ivarsgard for the raid.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had previously destroyed hives in Zenith, the strategy they now aim at the Bone Hives.

r.Karsk/Kopevnost: A bandit raid on Kosti, repelled by chance and Vigilance, triggered the campaign, and captains gathered at Kosti before the assault; Kosti's wise one Valya Sofyn Kosteva advised on confronting the horror in the Whispering Glade.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Thule warriors from Flajokep emerged from the Bonewood to fight the Druj and later withdrew back into it, vowing to defend only their own lands unless Imperial armies come.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Protected by the Dripping Echoes of the Fen, the vales of the Drownbark Forest decisively turned back the Druj after only minor skirmishes.
r.Ossium/Echofell: The Echofell fell to the Druj, the Tower of the Scorpion was gutted by fire and its garrison slain, the region keeps its under-threat quality, and only places like the Bone Hives still hold out.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: With Karsk's roads safe, the Galath Fields permanently lost their under-developed quality, and surviving Thule defenders fell back towards the region.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: Mentioned in passing: a Wooden Fastness raised in the heart of Nearweald offered sanctuary to Ossium's defenders.

Down that road.d: Freeborn Autumn magic, Summer citadels and the Empire's partial success at Rojota stopped the Corazón and Stephen of Sarcombe's Yegarra from seizing any mithril or white granite. The Hierro, Corazón and the zealous Escuta under Lefsnir Red-armed still took Nestor's Bounty and Jade Range with few deaths, offering Freeborn loyalty or exile and sending a flood of refugees into Madruga. Only one of Braydon's Jasse, Serra Briante or Serra Damata now stands between them and conquest. Heroes could destroy three runeboxes of tools to stop the orcs isolating the hill regions, kill Stephen to withdraw his Yegarra and bring Sarcombe's aid, or capture Meketh of the Flames to curse the Corazón.

n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun and their allies, including the Jotun orcs of Narkyst, now hold two fifths of Kahraman with few losses, and plan to wreck the hill roads and bridges of Serra Briante as the next step in their conquest.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn are losing Kahraman region by region: Fort Braydon is near breaking point, refugees flood into Madruga, and only Freeborn Autumn magic and the Empire's victory kept the Bourse mithril and white granite flowing this season.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is named as one source of emergency supplies for the defenders of Fort Braydon.
n.The Marches: Stephen of Sarcombe's Mournwold Yegarra have sworn to stay in Kahraman to avenge Wallis; if Stephen is killed and his head delivered to the Marcher egregore, the people of Sarcombe would send support to Fort Braydon.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Lefsnir Red-armed names the azure shores of the Bay of Catazar among the lands the Lasambrians mean to claim.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe's Yegarra chose to stay in Kahraman rather than return to Bregasland to support Mathilda Fisher.
t.Kahraman: Gambit and Jade Range fell to the Lasambrian Jotun, leaving only the northern hill regions in Imperial hands, with a battle opportunity to stop the orcs isolating them from one another.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: orcs who once lived in the passes overlooking Liathaven, now allied to the Lasambrians, lend their knowledge of Kahraman's high places.
t.Madruga: The stream of Kahraman refugees into Madruga became a flood, Madruga is a source of emergency supplies for Fort Braydon, and armies travelling to or from Segura must now pass through it.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold is a source of emergency supplies, and Sarcombe's residents would send aid to Fort Braydon if the traitor Stephen of Sarcombe's death is proved.
t.Segura: With Gambit and Jade Range lost, Imperial armies moving to or from Segura must go via Madruga, and the Corazón's new raiding prowess may stem from whatever the Lasambrians achieved there.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is listed as a source of emergency supplies for Fort Braydon.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Fort Braydon's garrison, cut off from the plains that fed it, is near breaking point; destroying even one runebox would prevent the orcs isolating Braydon's Jasse.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Lasambrian Jotun consolidated their hold on Gambit after taking Rojota, and launched their push into Jade Range from there.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: Jade Range fell after the decisive battle for Nestor's Bounty, its western settlements overwhelmed and its Freeborn offered loyalty or exile.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: The Great Mine's mithril was protected this season, but the orcs are gathering tools in the southern hills of Serra Briante to wreck its bridges and roads, making it the site of the coming battle.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Summer citadels guarded Serra Damata and the Damatian Cliffs' white granite reached the Empire, though Corazón raids may claim half its production next season and the region risks being isolated.

Every time it rains.d: No rain fell between the Spring Equinox and the Summer Solstice, so farms everywhere faced heavy losses; only Segura, protected by the Iron Qanat, and Skarsind, protected by Spring magic, were spared. The Imperial Breadbasket could stave off famine. During the Solstice, tempest jade could substitute for mana in several Spring rituals. Thunderous Deluge, Rivers of Life, Rivers Run Red or Regrow the Land's Heart cast on Casinea would affect the whole Empire, bringing floods, renewal, sickness or vallorn activity depending on the ritual. Other opportunities involved Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea on the Semmerlak, a cheaper permanent Call Down Lightning's Wrath, and Olic the Wanderer's offer of a ritual tome.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Culwich in Weirwater would suffer serious flooding under an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart. Semmerholm and Weirwater could also be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea to spread storms and farm-boosting rain around the Semmerlak.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Zenith and the Barrens, held by the Druj, are named among the non-Imperial territories that Imperial-regio rituals would not touch, leaving them simply to endure the drought.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Casinea, home of the Imperial regio, was the target through which certain rituals could be spread across the entire Empire during the conjunction.
n.Imperial Orcs: The farms of Skarsind were spared the drought thanks to the Spring enchantment placed on them at the Spring Equinox.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun-held Liathaven is named as a territory beyond the reach of the Imperial rituals, left to endure the drought.
n.Navarr: Empire-wide Rivers of Life or Rivers Run Red would energise the vallorn in Hercynia and especially Therunin, bringing more vallornspawn attacks or spreading miasma. Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart would also leave Eastring permanently marshy.
n.The Brass Coast: The farms of Segura were protected from the drought by the Iron Qanat, which kept the dry grasslands irrigated despite the crushing heat.
n.The League: Tassato faced the worst flooding if the Vassa burst its banks under Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart, and Sarvos some lesser flooding. Holberg risked flooding and Utterlund permanently becoming marsh.
n.The Marches: Marcher farms suffered the drought, though the Imperial Breadbasket's surplus and income could stave off famine and cushion Mitwold and Upwold. Meade risked serious flooding, while Bregasland, not counted as Imperial, would gain nothing from the rituals.
n.Thule: Any Empire-wide ritual would also affect the Thule orcs in their regions of Sermersuaq, Skarsind, Miekarova and Ossium, and the civil service advised the Ambassador to Otkodov to warn them, though flooding was unlikely to harm them.
n.Urizen: Olic the Wanderer offered to send the Concordance of Earthbound Stars to the Celestial Library if an Empire-wide curse ran its course, alongside an earlier offer to add it to Urizen lore for performing Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths.
n.Varushka: Karov, Karsk and Ossium were among the Semmerlak territories where Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea could be cast to batter shipping but bring farm-boosting rain to every territory around the lake.
n.Wintermark: Sermersuaq counted as an Imperial territory, so any Empire-wide curse or enchantment would reach it, including the regions held by Thule orcs there.

t.Bregasland: Because Bregasland could not elect a Senator that season, rituals cast through the Imperial regio would neither help nor harm it, and it had simply to endure the drought.
t.Brocéliande: As a non-Imperial territory, Brocéliande lay beyond the reach of the Imperial-regio rituals and would simply endure the drought.
t.Casinea: Casinea, where the Imperial regio lies, was the target through which Thunderous Deluge, Rivers of Life, Rivers Run Red or Regrow the Land's Heart could be spread across the whole Empire. Detect magic cast on the regio would reveal whether any had been used.
t.Hercynia: An Empire-wide Rivers of Life or Rivers Run Red would energise the vallorn in Hercynia, bringing increased vallornspawn attacks or a spread of miasma.
t.Holberg: Parts of Holberg would flood under an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart. As a Semmerlak territory, it could also be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea.
t.Karov: Karov was one of the Semmerlak territories that could be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea to spread storms and farm-boosting rain around the whole lake.
t.Karsk: Karsk was one of the Semmerlak territories that could be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea to spread storms and farm-boosting rain around the whole lake.
t.Liathaven: Held by the Jotun, Liathaven was outside the reach of the Imperial-regio rituals and would simply endure the drought.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova is listed among the territories where Thule orcs hold regions that any Empire-wide ritual would also affect.
t.Mitwold: Meade risked serious flooding under Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart, though the Imperial Breadbasket's income would help Mitwold absorb a lean autumn and winter.
t.Ossium: Ossium could be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea to spread storms around the Semmerlak, and Thule orcs holding regions there would feel any Empire-wide ritual.
t.Otkodov: The civil service advised the Ambassador to Otkodov to inform the orcs there of any Empire-wide magical effects that might reach Thule-held regions within the Empire.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos faced some flooding under an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge but was well prepared and expected to suffer minimal lasting damage.
t.Segura: Segura's farms were shielded from the drought by the Iron Qanat, which kept its grasslands irrigated through the heat.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm was one of the Semmerlak territories that could be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea to spread storms and farm-boosting rain around the whole lake.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq counted as Imperial, so any Empire-wide curse or enchantment would reach it, including the regions held by Thule orcs.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind's farms escaped the drought, receiving gentle healing rain from the Spring enchantment cast on them at the Spring Equinox.
t.Tassato: Tassato was expected to be hit worst if the Vassa burst its banks under an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart, causing extensive damage to the city.
t.The Barrens: Held by the Druj, the Barrens were beyond the reach of the Imperial-regio rituals and would simply endure the drought.
t.Therunin: Therunin's vallorn would be especially energised by an Empire-wide Rivers of Life or Rivers Run Red, bringing vallornspawn attacks or spreading miasma. Flooding from the Feverwater threatened Eastring.
t.Upwold: The Imperial Breadbasket's income was expected to help Upwold absorb the shock of a lean autumn and winter after the drought.
t.Weirwater: The town of Culwich faced serious floods under Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart. As a Semmerlak territory, Weirwater could also be targeted with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea.
t.Zenith: Held by the Druj, Zenith was outside the reach of the Imperial-regio rituals and would simply endure the drought.

r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund would be so saturated by an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart that the Morass would spread, permanently adding the marsh quality to the forest. Hallow of the Green World cast under the conjunction would certainly have the same result.
r.Therunin/Eastring: If the Feverwater rose under an Empire-wide Thunderous Deluge or Regrow the Land's Heart, Eastring would permanently gain the marsh quality.

Improve Walls of Holberg.d: The commission required 100 wains of white granite, 200 crowns in labour costs and six months to build. Funding came from many individual citizens between the Autumn Equinox of 384YE and the Autumn Equinox of 385YE. Jonah Yakovitch and Landon Hawcombe were the largest early donors, and others included Lula Kleist von Ennerlund, Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg and Doctor Luther Manfredi von Holberg. By Autumn 385YE the recorded granite donations totalled 100 wains. Once complete, the strength of the Walls of Holberg fortification would rise to 15,000.

n.The League: A League senator proposed the expansion of one of the League's major city fortifications, and many League citizens, a number bearing the von Holberg or van Holberg name, paid for it with their own money and granite.

t.Holberg: Holberg's walls were to be expanded so that, once finished, the fortification's strength would rise to 15,000, with the cost met largely by Holberg's own citizens.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Holfried is the region attached to the Walls of Holberg, and the commissioned expansion would raise the fortification's strength to 15,000 once complete.

In good company.d: Nearly fifty thousand alliance troops assaulted about thirty-five thousand Jotun at the mithril mine, which fell after a week. The Thule Shard of Winter then seized several hundred thralls and their mithril, angering many Winterfolk. The Suaq Wastes fell next, and more than four thousand died across the campaign. Sermersuaq became Imperial again, but the Senate must still assign it to a nation and allocate the mine. Igya Olgafsdottir was upgrading Olgafsdottirshal and the Fortress of Kalant. Heroes could destroy the Stonetoothed Obelisks to delay the work, kill Jotun champions Eisa Winterborn or Yanya Uranduln, rescue a Thule warlock or a hylje hostage, or intercept a spear meant for Hayaak.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm, whose general voiced disgust at fighting alongside slavers, helped break the Jotun line at the mine. The Weigher of Worth was asked by Jaheris's heralds to arrange the interception of the Spear of Bounty.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost the Pride of Ikka's Tears and the Suaq Wastes, along with many thralls and much mithril taken by the Thule. They fell back to strongly fortified halls in Tanikipari and Stark that Igya Olgafsdottir was racing to expand.
n.The Marches: The Marcher army the Drakes fought in the assault on Suaq Fount, its general framing the campaign as a way to draw Jotun forces away from Bregasland.
n.Thule: Three enchanted Thule armies and the garrison of the Citadel of Silver and Bone were the deciding factor in the victory. They also enslaved Jotun thralls and kept seized mithril, and they needed the Empire to recover the captured warlock Hustavok if they were to enchant their armies this season.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks helped retake the Suaq homeland, and Wintermark heroes cleared the last defenders from the mine. Sermersuaq and the mithril mine still awaited Senate assignment and allocation, while the hylje's continued aid to Wintermark depended on rescuing Koskinen.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes' general said fighting the Jotun in Sermersuaq would help save Marcher land unless the Jotun drew forces from Bregasland.
t.Hahnmark: The artisans of Runegrott rallied the people of Hahnmark to create up to six ritual staffs, a gift from Wintermark for the battle in Tanikipari.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the alliance was described as being between the Empire and Otkodov, and Thule strategy and concerns were to go through the Ambassador to Otkodov.
t.Sermersuaq: Spring magic kept the land flourishing as the alliance retook Suaq Fount and Suaq Wastes, making the territory Imperial once more. The Jotun still held Tanikipari and Stark, and losing a single region would cost the Empire the territory again.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the hylje had helped Imperial units escape after the earlier raid on Skallahn, and Koskinen was captured while doing so.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun siege engineer Igya Olgafsdottir is the eldest child of the Jarl of Tromsa.
t.Tsirku: A Jotun party under the ghodi Allok Surefoot had recovered the Spear of Bounty from the Grave of the Giants, an ice-cavern on the shore of Nutjuitoq, intending to give it to Hayaak.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule Citadel of Silver and Bone supplied Summer-touched warriors to the alliance, and the captured thralls and mithril were sent back there. Because the Thule hold these peaks, the Empire's grip on Sermersuaq remained precarious.
