r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The retreating Jotun fell back here, where work on the Fortress of Kalant was too far advanced to stop. Conjunctions led to the Flat Hills to recover Hustavok and to White Plume Rocks, where Koskinen was held.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: After a week-long assault the alliance captured the Pride of Ikka's Tears, freeing several dozen Suaq miners. The mine was left empty of mithril, and the Senate must now decide whether it will be Imperial or national.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Ominous northern lights blazed over the Wastes as the alliance overran newly built Jotun villages and drove the orcs out, with the Thule taking any thralls left behind as slaves.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: The alliance took outlying areas but stalled before Igya Olgafsdottir's fortified halls, including Olgafsdottirshal. A battle was offered to destroy the Stonetoothed Obelisks, delay its expansion, and possibly capture and complete the castle for the Empire.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Mentioned in passing: the hylje scout Koskinen was captured while leading Wintermark heroes out of Greenwall.

Into the valley.d: Three Dawnish armies and the Varushkan Golden Axe advanced from the Morass, while the Iron Helms, Northern Eagle and Wolves of War came up the Tarn Valley. More than thirty-five thousand Imperial troops faced only the garrison of the rebuilt Towers of Dusk and Druj enchantments. Despite the Rivers Run Red curse, casualties were negligible, and the armies met in northern Hope's Rest. The Iron Helms waged a merciless assault and the Wolves of War plundered. Conjunctions offered a Great Forest Orc reconciliation at Dourfell Keep, recovery of the Staff of Conviction, use of a Night regio, a Spring horror in the Bleaks, a cursed treasure trap, a threatened bridge and a chance to flood the Fangs.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun, Gryphon's Pride and Hounds of Glory spearheaded the conquest of the Carmine Fields, and Dawnish generals may order a triumphant charge here under Tobias Field's mandate. The Great Forest Orcs offer a reconciliation ceremony with the Dawnish, while a released Spring beast threatens around three hundred Dawnish casualties.
n.Druj: The Druj lost the Carmine Fields and Hope's Rest, defended only by the Towers of Dusk garrison and their enchantments. They laid traps including a cursed treasure, a released Spring horror and a plan to destroy the Singing River bridge.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the oppressive aura of Grendel-held Spiral is compared to the aura around Dourfell Keep.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: if the reconciliation succeeds, Imperial troops could move secretly between the Eaves of Peytaht and Highguard-held Reikos.
n.Navarr: The southern armies advanced out of Navarr's Therunin, and the Navarr vate Drustan Brocs Guard proposed using Align the Celestial Net to turn the Night regio to Spring or Summer magic. The Great Forest Orcs had first offered to help the Navarr fight in the Barrens.
n.The League: The Wolves of War, swelled by mercenaries and Temeschwari bravos, plundered Druj garrisons in Hope's Rest. A cursed treasure now threatens the loss of two hundred and fifty strength and no plunder orders before 386YE Winter.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: several generals said their aim was to open a route south and help liberate Zenith for Urizen.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe, Iron Helms and Northern Eagle fought from both north and south, meeting in northern Hope's Rest, and Varushkan physicks helped keep casualties low. The Golden Axe vanguard now risks around three hundred deaths if Druj ritualists destroy the Singing River bridge.

t.Holberg: The Golden Sun, Gryphon's Pride, Hounds of Glory and Golden Axe launched their invasion from Holberg, and the causeway lets armies withdraw north into it.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-created insurgent advantage in Ossium is cited as the model for the allied insurgents Hope's Rest could gain.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orc guides could let Imperial troops travel unexpectedly between the Eaves of Peytaht and Reikos.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Emerald Harvester clan guarding Dourfell Keep originally came from Sarangrave.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral's unique oppression is compared to the Dourfell aura, and the magicians of Spiral Castle supplied the 'Dark Clouds Gather' arcane projection.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwari bravos joined the Wolves of War seeking profit from the war against the Druj.
t.The Barrens: The Empire conquered the Carmine Fields and Hope's Rest, cutting the territory in half and confining the Druj largely to the east. Several conjunctions offered chances to secure that presence or blunt Druj traps.
t.Therunin: The Iron Helms, Northern Eagle and Wolves of War marched into the Barrens through the Tarn Valley, and armies can now return south into Therunin. The Great Forest Orcs sheltering there offer reconciliation and support.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater is not named directly; the page concerns Dawnish armies campaigning in the Barrens.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish and Varushkan generals described the push as opening a route south to help free Zenith.

r.Holberg/The Morass: Mentioned in passing: the northern Imperial armies marched into the Barrens out of the Morass.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Gryphon's Pride scouts probed Bitter Strand without attacking, finding the Saltmaw Spring regio from which a ritual could flood the Fangs' mithril mines for at least two seasons.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Mentioned in passing: with the central regions taken, the Druj are expected to struggle to hold Dawnguard.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are expected to find the Heart of Peytaht difficult to hold once the centre fell.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Hope's Rest fell to the Empire as northern and southern armies met in its foothills. At Dourfell Keep the Empire may reconcile with the Great Forest Orcs, recover the Staff of Conviction for lasting insurgent support, and exploit a Night regio.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Mentioned in passing: Murderdale is named among regions the Druj will struggle to hold after the causeway.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Saltmarsh's marshes teem with Druj enchantments. The proposed 'Dark Clouds Gather' ritual would drown much of it, turning it coastal and preventing a Druj fortification there for a year.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: Druj raiders struck from the Bleaks, and Druj ghulai have released a Spring horror in its Lupine Arbour that the Knight Protector of Spring is expected to stop.
r.The Barrens/The Carmine Fields: The Dawnish armies and Golden Axe conquered the Carmine Fields across open ground. A conjunction to the Red Plains offers a chance to seize cursed Druj treasure afflicting the Wolves of War.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: The Towers of Dusk loom over the Plains of Teeth, rebuilt and heavily reinforced, and their garrison provided the only Druj troops opposing the Empire.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: Mentioned in passing: Druj raiders melted back into the Untrod Groves, now within the eastern half left to the orcs.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The recovered Staff of Conviction can be sent to the Lower Tarn Valley via Anvil, and Great Forest Orc hunters there will leave to establish a free spy network in the Barrens.

Make a deal.d: Three opportunities arose. Thornsong House, a Senate-commissioned weirwood college at Peakedge Song, would create the Thornsinger title and allow research into new potions. Expanding the Feverwater docks into a fortified steading would let the Dredgemaster push into Sarangrave and Zenith waters, raid the shores, and offer Navarr an Adventure in the Sarangrave. The Great Forest Orcs offered cheaper herb garden upgrades in Therunin. If the Senate promised to cede them the Heart of Peytaht during this Solstice, they would extend that aid to other Navarr territories and permanently enrich the Thimble. A Sentinel Gate conjunction also opened onto a Feverwater wreck, while outlaws troubled East Ashes.

n.Druj: Druj raiders harry the Feverwater shores and hold a settlement in Bloodwater Marsh. The proposed docks expansion would let armed boats push into Druj-dominated waters and raid their shores, while outlaws in East Ashes already raid the Druj in Zenith.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Peakedge Stead owes much of its size to lingering Highborn exiles, it is popular with Highborn healers, and it trades with the herb gardens of Reikos.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: some of the East Ashes outlaws are said to be Navarr displaced from Liathaven, which the Jotun hold.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were offered a prestigious herb-lore college with a Thornsinger chosen by their herb garden owners, an expanded Feverwater operation, and an Adventure in the Sarangrave open only to Navarr units. Great Forest Orc help would also make upgrading herb gardens cheaper, nation-wide if the Senate made its promise.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: reasonable roads link Peakedge Stead to Highwatch in Morrow, bringing Imperial merchants to trade.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: recent events in Varushka have left some Therunin steadings nervous about the outlaw gang in East Ashes.

t.Brocéliande: If the Senate promised the Heart of Peytaht to the Great Forest Orcs, their woodshapers would visit even Brocéliande to help expand herb gardens. Some of the East Ashes outlaws are said to be Navarr displaced from there.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia's herb gardens would gain the Great Forest Orcs' help, cutting upgrade costs by one wain of weirwood per rank, but only if the Senate made its promise over the Heart of Peytaht.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: some of the outlaws troubling East Ashes are former Navarr displaced from Liathaven.
t.Miaren: The excitement over Seren in Miaren highlighted how undeveloped Therunin remains. Miaren's herb gardens would also benefit from the orcs' woodshaping if the Senate made its promise over the Heart of Peytaht.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: a reasonable road links Highwatch in Morrow to Peakedge Stead in Therunin.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Peakedge Stead lies on the border with Reikos, is linked to High Chalcis by road, and trades with Reikos's herb gardens.
t.Sarangrave: Expanded Feverwater docks would let Imperial boats dredge and raid the Sarangrave half of the lake, and would serve as a staging point for Navarr adventurers heading up its river. The Senate might later appraise using the docks to help invade the territory.
t.The Barrens: The Great Forest Orcs asked the Senate to commit, at this Solstice only, to ceding the Heart of Peytaht to them once the Barrens becomes Imperial.
t.Therunin: Therunin was the focus of all the proposals: Thornsong House at Peakedge, a fortified steading at the Feverwater docks, cheaper herb garden upgrades and a richer Thimble. The territory also faces unresolved questions over the Lost Liao Garden salvage and a growing outlaw problem.
t.Zenith: Feverwater boats could push into occupied Zenith if the docks were expanded. Outlaws based in East Ashes already raid the Druj there, and would need new targets if the Druj were driven out.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The river feeding the Sarangrave runs through the vallorn heart of Bendol, part of the route the proposed Navarr adventurers would take from the Feverwater docks.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: The Bloodwater Spears orc sept lives along the eastern banks here. Raiding boats would need to give the Druj settlement in the marsh a wide berth, though paid thorns could push into its Druj-dominated waters.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The river from the Feverwater runs up through Nesustak Forest, opening it to Navarr adventurers if the docks were expanded.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: Turan Flats lies along the river route that Navarr adventurers could follow from an expanded Feverwater docks.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Great Forest Orcs, who long tended the weirwood grove of the Eaves of Peytaht here, asked the Senate to promise them the region once the Barrens is conquered.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: East Ashes holds the ancient Feverwater docks, proposed for expansion into a fortified steading, and the submerged wreck reached by a Sentinel Gate conjunction. An outlaw gang is harassing travellers on its southern trods.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Great Forest Orcs' herb gardens and potion-brewing skill in the Lower Tarn Valley underpin the Thornsong House plan and their offer of cheaper herb garden upgrades. The region's briars are still awaiting a decision on the Lost Liao Garden salvage.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Peakedge Song would host Thornsong House, a Senate-commissioned weirwood college meant to make it the Empire's foremost centre of herb lore, overseen by a new Thornsinger.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: The vallorn of Sweetglades shapes where East Ashes steadings are built. The Lost Liao Garden, whose salvage remains undecided, was found just outside the region.

Make it happen.d: Graciana identified three septs able to fight: the Bloodwater Spears under Halyx Fireeyes, the Water Walkers under the blind Agoska, and the human Grynbor under Queen Olwenna. Arming each would take a Senate motion, six months, 100 wains of mithril and 50 thrones, yielding a green army of 3,000 strength. Their morale, rated craven, would have to rise to resolved before they would revolt. Options to raise it included the Winter Sun's Break the Chains order, arming all three septs, treaties of military support or independence, and visible defeats of the Druj. Naomi and Lutomysla proposed diplomatic and magical alternatives. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered a chance to rescue a captured Bloodwater Spear from Druj torture.

n.Druj: The Druj clans ruling Sarangrave, the Thornwasp, Banded Snake and Marshlizard, face an Imperial appraisal of how their hated slave septs might be armed and emboldened to rise against them. Defeats in Zenith or the Barrens were named as ways to break the septs' fear of them.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr-held Therunin is named as the only Imperial territory bordering Sarangrave from which the Winter Sun could work to incite the septs.
n.The League: The Senator for Temeschwar proposed the motion behind the appraisal and was urged to gather heroes for the conjunction to save the captured Bloodwater Spear orc.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the recent capture of Ossium from the Druj is cited as a defeat too distant to inspire the Sarangrave septs, and Ossium's Sand Fishers as a people more broken than they are.

t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the taking of Ossium is cited as a crushing Imperial defeat of the Druj, though too far from Sarangrave to stir the septs, and its Sand Fishers are recalled as having been completely broken.
t.Sarangrave: The appraisal assessed whether Sarangrave's three septs could be secretly armed through the spy network and encouraged to revolt against Druj rule, which has gone unchallenged in living memory. A conjunction to Dead Stone Woods near the Feverwater offered a chance to rescue a tortured Bloodwater Spear.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's senator proposed the motion commissioning the appraisal, and the civil service suggested that same senator organise the heroes for the Dead Stone Woods conjunction.
t.Therunin: As the only Imperial territory bordering Sarangrave, Therunin is where the Winter Sun could stand while issuing Break the Chains to embolden a sept. Lutomysla also suggested a fane to Papa Otec on its border with Sarangrave.
t.Zenith: Driving the Druj from neighbouring Zenith was identified as a visible defeat that would raise the morale of the Sarangrave septs.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The human Grynbor sept makes regular forays into Bendol from neighbouring Nesustak Forest.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Bloodwater Marsh is home to the Bloodwater Spears, the largest of the three septs, whose spear-fishers could become a formidable force if armed and armoured.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: The Water Walkers, boatmen who ferry goods and people for the Druj, keep a number of small settlements in Kroll.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Nesustak Forest is home to the Grynbor, a human sept under Queen Olwenna that sends expeditions into the vallorn-infested forest near the ruins of Béantal Dol.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: The Water Walkers maintain small settlements on the Turan Flats, making the region one base of a sept the Empire might arm.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: The Bloodwater Spears, led by the short-tempered matriarch Halyx Fireeyes, live in the Whisperwood as well as Bloodwater Marsh.

Our thumping hearts.d: Barien's herald Revel would moderate the tag-team grand melee alongside the Archmage of Summer and the Master of Ice and Darkness. Teams were three magicians, armed only with implements, with no potions, vis or crystal mana once fighting began, and no killing. Champions were announced for Meraud, Cathan Canae, Jaheris, Adamant, Prospero, Sadogua and others. Eleonaris, Hayaak, Zakalwe and Wise Rangara kept their teams obscure or still recruiting. A Highborn team sought to keep the college free of any patron, and Agramant, though under enmity, offered rewards to anyone who fought for him. The result would stand until 387YE at the earliest.

n.Dawn: The tourney was to be held in the Dawnish Glory Square. Tristan Wolfborn fought for Meraud, while Jaheris's team was entirely Dawnish: Senators Zadkiel de Coeurdefer and Bohemond de Rondell, with Drake de Coeurdefer.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: in the opening tale, a Freeborn hakima coven had fled the Bay of Catazar because of the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highborn magicians fielded two teams. Ahzrukhal chose Aemon and Ingrid, daughter of Jan, to champion Sadogua, and Baalam, Isolde and Gideon fought to keep the Icy Crag free of any eternal patron.
n.Navarr: Cedric Gallows of Navarr was one of Meraud's three champions, and Zakalwe's undisclosed team was said to include a Navarr magician.
n.The Brass Coast: Rhianos sought to recruit Freeborn battle magicians with the most exciting adventures to fight on its behalf, and Esteban i DelRio Blanco i Guerra was among Cathan Canae's champions.
n.Urizen: Sejanus of Urizen was the only one of Adamant's original champions still available and was charged with recruiting two more, while Zakalwe's team reportedly included an Urizen magician.
n.Wintermark: Tiberius the Rainmage fought for Meraud, and the Kallavesi Runar Hval of Raven's Hold was one of Cathan Canae's chosen champions.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Bohemond de Rondell, Senator for Astolat and throne aspirant, was named as one of Jaheris's champions.
t.Bay of Catazar: In the opening tale, a lone hakima who had stayed behind when her coven fled the Grendel honoured an old compact with the Guardian of the Cloudsea. In return he promised that none of her family would drown in the Bay in the coming year.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the rest of Caita i Guerra's hakima coven had fled north to Madruga.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Zadkiel de Coeurdefer, Senator for Semmerholm, was named as one of Jaheris's champions.

Out of the realm.d: Seven magical fortifications were raised: Spring forests in Nearweald, ice castles in Kahraman against the Lasambrian Jotun, and mist castles in Bregasland, Ossium and Kallavesa. Penumbral Veils shrouded Ossium, Madruga, Kahraman, the Barrens and Zenith. Regrow the Land's Heart spared Skarsind from the Great Drought. The expanded College of Warcasting drew many Tamazi into the Imperial Orcs. Prospero's golden spiders began aiding Urizen's heliopticons and the Doyen of the Spires. Cathan Canae threatened to withdraw support if more land is ceded. Kaela will triple her grim legions for the Druj whenever the Suns of Couros steal them. Four of the Childer of the Black Drop were found dead in Vardstein Vale.

n.Dawn: Barien, Lord of the Crossroads, will hold a rewarding ceremony for challengers via the Semmerstones in Causse, a Dawnish region.
n.Druj: Penumbral Veils hide the Barrens and Zenith from divination. Kaela's grievance means nine cadres of grim legionnaires will fight alongside the Druj this season, while new Imperial fortifications in Ossium stand against them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: golden spiders descended on heliopticon towers in Grendel-held Spiral, and former Mareave gladiators are joining Skarsind's septs and its College of Warcasting.
n.Highguard: Kaela declared a bounty on the Highborn coven of the Suns of Couros. She will send three of her grim legionnaires against Highborn armies for every one they summon, unless one of the coven secures Imperial lore status for Abandon the Mortal Shackles.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind's farms were spared the Great Drought by Regrow the Land's Heart. The expanded College of Warcasting drew a wave of Tamazi to join the nation, though their bonecarvers remain cautious and plan to visit Anvil in Autumn.
n.Jotun: Two castles of ice and granite were raised in Kahraman to bolster Fort Braydon against the Lasambrian Jotun.
n.The Brass Coast: Kahraman was fortified with two castles of ice and granite, and Penumbral Veils now shroud both Kahraman and Madruga against divination.
n.The League: The bodies of four members of the Childer of the Black Drop, a League sorcerous cabal declared sorcerers in 354YE, were found in Vardstein Vale. Jodeya Watiker and the cabal's library remain missing.
n.The Marches: Castles of mist were raised over the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire in Bregasland.
n.Urizen: Prospero's golden spiders now aid Urizen's heliopticon towers and let the Doyen of the Spires speed codification for orichalcum, provided the resulting rituals stay out of Imperial lore. Agon also extended the chance to expand the Citadel of Highwatch to the end of the Summer Solstice.
n.Varushka: Ossium gained a Spring forest fortification in Nearweald and a mist castle in Drownbark Forest, and is shrouded by a Penumbral Veil. Wise Rangara will become patron of Marshstand Skerry if the Conclave asks her.
n.Wintermark: Restless Suaq spirits trouble Turelva in Hahnmark, and Kallavesa's West Marsh gained a mist castle. The Icewalkers are invited to perform before Barien to claim their reward, and his heralds will visit Lumi's.

t.Bregasland: Castles of mist now fortify the fens of the Rushes and Ottermire.
t.Hahnmark: Anguished ghosts of Frayed Suaq haunt the lands near Turelva, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction offers scops a chance to lay them to rest.
t.Kahraman: Two castles of ice and granite drawn from the Breath of Winter fortify the territory against the Lasambrian Jotun, and a Penumbral Veil hides it from scrying.
t.Kallavesa: A castle of mist was raised over the marsh of West Marsh.
t.Madruga: A Penumbral Veil now hangs over the territory, so rituals must overcome it to scry there.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: former Mareave gladiators living in Skarsind benefit from its enchantment and are joining the College of Warcasting.
t.Morrow: Golden spiders from the Autumn realm descended on Morrow's heliopticon towers, making message-sending faster and more reliable.
t.Ossium: The territory gained a Spring forest fortification and a mist castle, and lies under a Penumbral Veil. Wise Rangara awaits the Conclave's invitation to become patron of Marshstand Skerry.
t.Redoubt: Golden spiders settled at Redoubt's working heliopticon towers to assist their Urizen operators.
t.Semmerholm: Barien summons challengers to the Semmerstones in Causse, from where they may pass to the Grove of Thousands for his rewarding ceremony.
t.Skarsind: Regrow the Land's Heart brought gentle rain that spared its farms from the Great Drought. The expanded College of Warcasting was flooded with Tamazi, young orcs and former gladiators.
t.Spiral: Golden spiders descended even on the functioning heliopticon towers in Spiral.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: two members of the Childer of the Black Drop were of Tassato Mestra.
t.Temeschwar: Scouts found four long-missing sorcerers of the Childer of the Black Drop dead in a cottage in Vardstein Vale, a mystery that has baffled the magistrates.
t.The Barrens: A Penumbral Veil shrouds the Druj-held Barrens against divination.
t.Zenith: A Penumbral Veil shrouds Druj-held Zenith against divination.

r.Bregasland/Ottermire: A castle of mist was raised over the fens of Ottermire.
r.Hahnmark/Bruckland: Restless spirits wail near Turelva, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction at 23:00 on Saturday lets up to fifty performers reach the woodland to calm them.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: A castle of ice and granite was raised here to help fortify Kahraman against the Lasambrian Jotun.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: A castle of ice and granite was raised here to fortify Kahraman.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: A castle of mist now fortifies the marsh of West Marsh.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: A castle of mist was raised over the bogs of Drownbark Forest.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: A Spring realm fortification strengthened the forests of Nearweald against Druj depredations.
r.Semmerholm/Causse: A conjunction at 2pm on Saturday will lead challengers through the Semmerstones to Barien's ceremony of rewarding.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Mentioned in passing: Padik Tarvin and the still-missing Jodeya Watiker of the Childer of the Black Drop hailed from Tassato Mestra.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: Scouts near Lorenzo's Deep Pockets found four sorcerers dead in a cottage, with a fifth place set at the table and an empty rune-inlaid trunk.

Received with a strange delight.d: Alexander of Axos sought private meetings, while the Bastion herbalist Nain of Gamul's Gate urged the Synod, healers and Conclave to scrutinise untested foreign drugs such as the Unwound Coil. Around fifteen Axou claiming Terunael descent travelled the trods and planned to show a relic lekythos to the Navarr vates. Two Free Mark fighters, with the Stormcrow Aedwin the Weaver, sought guidance on their skeins. The Urizeni refugees Eucleus and Valerius pursued the Hand of Guerra, and Valerius planned to sell an heirloom. Maistir Comyn and Lir rushed to Anvil over a danger linked to the evacuation of Feroz. Ezra Von Sarvos of the Silver Frame Carta intended to call on the High Bard.

n.Grendel: The Grendel trader Maistir Comyn and his bodyguard Lir hurried to Anvil on an emergency apparently connected with the evacuation of Feroz, claiming someone was in terrible danger and that a Cardinal would hear of any delay.
n.Highguard: The Highborn coast and roads saw the Grendel ship's hurried arrival at Crown's Quay and its crew's dash through Necropolis toward Casinea, while the Bastion herbalist Nain of Gamul's Gate led calls to scrutinise foreign narcotics and medicines.
n.Jotun: As the Empire reclaimed dominion over Sermersuaq from Jotun occupation, the Free Mark fighters who had waged a brutal sabotage campaign against the Jotun began returning home.
n.Navarr: Axou travellers claiming Terunael descent visited wayhouses across the southern trods seeking out the Navarr, some adopting Navarr dress, and planned to bring their relic to the Navarr woods entrance at Anvil to show the vates and the citizens who had helped them.
n.The Brass Coast: The House of Guerra in Calvos took in a party of Urizeni refugees, two of whom set off after the Hand of Guerra and could be found in the Brass Coast encampment, while the Grendel visitors headed for the Freeborn camp.
n.The League: Ezra Von Sarvos, the ageing Merchant Prince of the Silver Frame Carta, a Sarvosan guild of art dealers, made a rare journey out of Sarvos to call on the new High Bard.
n.Urizen: A spire-in-exile of Urizeni refugees reached the House of Guerra, with the philosopher Eucleus chasing the Hand of Guerra and Valerius seeking to sell a family heirloom to fund a new life far from Urizen, while the High Bard was to receive Ezra Von Sarvos in the Urizen camp.
n.Wintermark: Former Free Mark resistance fighters, dogged by rumours of dark pacts and Frayed skeins, returned to their homes, and two of them came to Anvil with the Stormcrow Aedwin the Weaver to seek guidance on their skeins.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the herbalist Nain of Gamul's Gate claimed to make the best Feverfail Elixir in Bastion.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the Axou travellers of Terunael descent unsurprisingly avoided visiting Brocéliande.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Maistir Comyn and Lir hurried through Necropolis toward Casinea on their way to Anvil.
t.Feroz: The Grendel traders' urgent errand was said to concern the evacuation of Feroz, prompting speculation about the fate of the few human citizens left there.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the Axou travellers seeking the Navarr had so far avoided visiting Hercynia.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the Axou travellers unsurprisingly avoided visiting Liathaven.
t.Madruga: A bedraggled party of Urizeni refugees arrived at the House of Guerra in Calvos seeking sanctuary.
t.Necropolis: A Grendel ship docked in a rush at Crown's Quay without tariff paperwork, its captain's attempts to pay off questioners annoying the civil servants until a young crew member filled out the forms and faced the local magistrate.
t.Sarvos: The Silver Frame Carta, an old Sarvosan art-dealing guild with a shady reputation but generous patronage, saw its rarely travelling Merchant Prince leave the city for Anvil.
t.Sermersuaq: With the Empire reclaiming Sermersuaq, former thralls were freed and surviving Free Mark fighters began rebuilding homes scarred by occupation amid suspicion and gossip from their neighbours.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Axou travellers seeking the Navarr had so far avoided visiting Therunin.

r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: The House of Guerra's hostel in Calvos sheltered a group of tired Urizeni refugees, whose philosopher Eucleus left almost at once in pursuit of the absent Hand of Guerra.

Repair Blood Red River Museum.d: Proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Temeschwar, the self-funded motion commissioned repairs costing 15 wains of white granite, 15 wains of weirwood and 150 crowns in labour and art, taking three months. Several citizens donated over the following seasons. Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato provided most of it after Spring Equinox 385YE: 17 thrones, 1 crown, 18 rings and all the materials. The museum remains a great work of Pride. The motion intended the Curator to be a League citizen chosen unanimously by the League senators. Because the title carries votes in the Synod, that method was ruled impossible, and the Senate passed a Constitutional Court motion clarifying this. The Curator was to be appointed at Summer Solstice 385YE.

n.The League: League citizens, led by Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato, funded the restoration of one of their nation's great works of Pride. However, the League senators lost the power to choose the new Curator by unanimous vote, because the title carries Synod votes.

t.Tassato: The Blood Red River Museum in Tassato was repaired and rebuilt, remaining a great work of Pride. A new Imperial title, Curator of the Blood Red River, was created for it, with the appointment due at Summer Solstice 385YE.

Roll and fall.d: Muireall hired Broken Shore moridun, bought a map of Tsark from Axos and recruited Kaban sappers to cross from Ossuary in Spiral into Naucini and Borenj, seeking loot, white granite and mithril. She offered 7 crowns per unit plus loot and a lottery of wains. Knight-Marshal Louis du Baselard's Gilded Sceptre vowed to hold an undermanned guard post; a Purple Sails faction would pay defenders 5 crowns, hoping for diplomatic ties with Tsark. Because everyone involved was foreign, the Senate had to permit involvement on both sides. Without intervention the raid would reach Borenj and take some white granite. Competing Synod mandates were proposed.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj conquest of Dawnguard cost the Gilded Sceptre everything, and the Purple Sails looked to Zenith or Spiral being retaken from them.
n.Grendel: Paymaster Muireall staked her fortune on the raid. Its success would encourage further Grendel joint ventures with the Empire, while Imperial opposition would damage relations and could ruin her.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Grendel recruiters bought drinks for potential mercenaries in the taverns of Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: some Imperial Orcs questioned attacking a people among whom orcs and humans seemed to live in harmony.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Tom Keeper's mandate urged captains to ignore Tsark and raid Jotun-held Skallahn instead.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Grendel agents recruited in the paradors of Madruga.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: recruiters visited Sarvos guildhalls, and League Free Companies argued that mercenary work was simply mercenary work.
n.Urizen: Two rival Urizen Assembly mandates were proposed: Herminius urged joining the raid to encourage trade with the Grendel, while Able the Taller urged sentinels to retake Zenith instead.
n.Varushka: Varushkan wagon raiders argued that Tsark's wealth was fair game, and General Assembly mandates would only sway Varushkan units with a greater majority.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: some in Wintermark considered protecting the people of Tsark more heroic than robbing them.

t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Muireall's agents offered drinks and the raid opportunity in Madruga's paradors.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the raid was organised by an entrepreneur of the North Mareave Trading Consortium.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Tsark's homeland faced a Grendel-led raid on Naucini, Borenj and possibly Kamen Quarry. How far it penetrated depended on whether Imperial units joined the raiders or defended the passes.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Grendel recruiters sought Imperial mercenaries in Necropolis's taverns.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Muireall's agents recruited in the inns of Redoubt.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Grendel agents pitched the raid in Sarvos's guildhalls.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: Tom Keeper's proposed mandate urged captains to raid Skallahn rather than intervene in Tsark.
t.Spiral: Spiral was the staging ground: Imperial units would gather at Ossuary, porters would carry loot back there, and Salt Lord Kaliact would only allow passage if raiding were also legal.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Able the Taller's mandate urged Urizeni forces to retake Zenith instead, and the Purple Sails hoped for its return to Imperial hands.

r.Mountains of the Moon/Borenj: Borenj was the raid's ultimate target. By default the raiders would plunder it for white granite, and a strong raid could reach Kamen Quarry.
r.Mountains of the Moon/Naucini: Raiders planned to bypass the Mislitel Pass into Naucini, and with enough strength could loot Krug and the Disc of the Ogledano.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Ossuary was the assembly point where Imperial units would meet the mercenaries before crossing the peaks east.

Shimmerglisten.d: The Empire's surprise was spoiled by a letter signed by Watt of Lambrooke, Senator Travid Longest Path and General Lleu Tarw. The Feni chose to talk instead. Urhalin, who loathes Terunael, agreed to lure the Heirs in if no Feni were harmed. The ninety Heirs were massacred, but Druss escaped to the vallorn's heart. Urhalin then asked the Empire to withdraw. She declared the Feni would seize Liaven's Glen, named Watt their contact, and offered to send envoys to Anvil about the curse. Navarr were offered competing Synod mandates on whether to abandon Terunael's legacy. The vallorn remains a lurking threat of up to 15,000.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a smattering of Dawnish allies joined the Navarr-led force that surrounded Hotters Mire.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn allies were among the smaller contingents in the force sent into Liathaven.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named on the page; the events took place in Liathaven, which they held at the time.
n.Navarr: Navarr thorns led the stealthy encirclement and the slaughter of the Heirs, and their own General Lleu Tarw co-signed the warning to the Feni. The Navarr Assembly now faced rival mandates on whether to forsake the legacy of Terunael, which would win Feni goodwill at the cost of historical research.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark allies were among the smaller contingents accompanying the Navarr into Liathaven.

t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is noted as home to at least one large group of Feni who might respond to a Navarr shift away from Terunael.
t.Liathaven: Imperial forces destroyed the Heirs of Terunael at Hotters Mire, ending their attempt to break the curse there. The Feni now plan to claim more land, while the vallorn's heart remains a regenerating threat of up to 15,000.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Travid Longest Path, Senator for Therunin, was one of the three signatories of the letter that warned the Feni.

r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: Urhalin warned the Empire that the Feni of Hotters Mire intended to seize Liaven's Glen by force and make the whole region their home.

Take it further.d: Half the Imperial nations shunned the Spring raid, but around forty captains and warleaders from Highguard, the League, the Marches, Wintermark and the Imperial Orcs plundered Skallahn as far as Iron Stand, Bjarkey and Ulfrsmoor before withdrawing safely. They secured no Bourse resources and did no strategic damage. A Summer raid by fleets and military units, aimed at military targets and sparing graves and shrines, could achieve tiered results depending on its total strength. These ranged from overrunning Greenwall to looting Eyrarfell's Shining Caverns, while strong enough fleets could burn the Kongegőr causeway or reach the Sea of Snow. Spring veterans gained a bonus. Wintermark and the Marches could jointly name a Marshal, and House Oddsboy and the hylje offered further aid.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Killian Mortére's mandate urged the Dawnish not to take part in the Spring raid.
n.Highguard: Highborn ship captains helped carry Imperial forces safely to Greenwall in Spring, and the seven Highguard participants would gain a bonus if they joined the Summer raid.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orcs led by Ergot pressed deep into Skallahn during the Spring raid, which would give them a veterans' advantage in any return.
n.Jotun: The Jotun Jarls drove off the Spring raiders but grew overconfident. A strong Summer raid could scatter several Jarls, plunder their mines and stores, damage the Kongegőr causeway and disrupt the resupply and raising of their armies.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr assembly, at first supportive, endorsed Meredith Nighthaven in renouncing the Spring raid as unwise.
n.The League: A handful of League companies joined the Spring raid, and their six citizens would gain the veterans' bonus if they returned to Skallahn.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly's guidance to strike only military targets shaped the Summer raid, and Marcher fleets could operate in the Gullet at full strength. Jointly naming a Marshal with Wintermark and honouring House Oddsboy's captains could bring more ships to the raid and possibly a permanent Gullet raiding option for Marcher fleets.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Lochias's mandate urged the Urizen not to take part in the Spring raid.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk supplied the largest share of the Spring raiders, and Wintermark fleets could sail the Gullet without penalty. The assembly could name a Marshal jointly with the Marches, the hylje offered further aid, and the Westerhal fisherfolk stood to gain new fishing grounds.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the earlier mapping of the Bay was cited as the model for any future scouting of the Sea of Snow.
t.Hordalant: If 10,000 strength of fleets burned the Kongegőr causeway linking Skallahn and Hordalant, Jotun armies crossing between the two would have to halt on arrival for at least six months.
t.Kallavesa: If at least 5,000 strength of fleets supported the raid, Westerhal's fisherfolk could fish the rich Jotun-held waters of the Gullet under Winterfolk escort and bring prosperity to western Kallavesa.
t.Mitwold: Jarvey "Strongoar" Oddsboy of Steward's Landing near Odd's End pledged 1,000 strength to the raid. With 5,000 strength of fleets, the village could become a permanent staging post for Marcher raids on the Kalsea coast.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Lazarus of the Necropolis is listed among the Highguard participants in the Spring raid.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Uberto Alessandri di Caricomare vacino a Sarvos is listed among the League participants in the Spring raid.
t.Sea of Snow: If fleets reached 12,500 strength, they could push into the Sea of Snow, letting the Senate commission voyages at the Autumn Equinox to map the coasts west of the Empire.
t.Sermersuaq: Overrunning Greenwall would stop the Jotun resupplying the Fortress of Kalant in Stark if they lost Tanikipari. A Sentinel Gate conjunction to the Floes of Tokusok, technically in the Suaq Wastes, offered the chance to recruit the hylje's bloodthirsty cousins.
t.Skallahn: Skallahn was raided in Spring without lasting effect, and faced a second raid whose results ranged from overrunning Greenwall to looting the Shining Caverns of Eyrarfell. After this season the Jotun would be ready, ruling out another grand raid for a year or so.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The fisherfolk of Westerhal in the West Marsh helped ferry warriors and could, with enough fleet escort, win a permanent opportunity to fish the rich western and northern Gullet.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: If Greenwall were overrun and the Jotun lost Tanikipari, they could not resupply the Fortress of Kalant in Stark until the Spring Equinox 385YE without giving the Empire a battle opportunity.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The Floes of Tokusok, only technically part of the Suaq Wastes, were the Sentinel Gate destination where the Mediator of Hyljehal might secure 1,000 strength from the hylje's estranged cousins.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: A Jotun loss of Tanikipari, combined with an overrun Greenwall, would cut off resupply to the Fortress of Kalant in Stark.
r.Skallahn/Bjarkey: Mentioned in passing: some Spring raiders got as far as Bjarkey before being forced to retreat.
r.Skallahn/Eyrarfell: With 15,000 strength the raid could breach Eyrarfell against Jarl Gilla Sverrisdóttir's ulvenwar and plunder her mines. At 20,000 it could loot the Shining Caverns mithril mine and threaten the Steelweaver's Crucible, denying Jotun armies natural resupply for two seasons.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Spring raiders landed safely in Greenwall. With 5,000 to 10,000 strength, a Summer raid could overrun its forges and mines, scatter Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard and burn his hall, and make Greenwall easier to capture until the end of the Autumn Equinox 385YE.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: Spring raiders reached Iron Stand. With 10,000 strength, a Summer raid could defeat Jarl Ebbe of Overgaard and Jarl Alvilda Ottesen and plunder the Broken Chasm for white granite, crippling Jotun emergency resupply for two seasons.
r.Skallahn/Ulfrsmoor: Raiders would spare the temple of Ulfrskelf and the market town of Overgaard. With 12,500 strength they could storm Jarl Ottesen's fortified hall and empty his storehouses, cheapening Imperial spy networks across Kalsea.

The day writes the words.d: Dawnish armies led the Empire's invasion, but tallies credited Varushka with 45.3% of land taken, Dawn 41.8% and the League 12.9%. The General Assembly upheld a mandate rejecting the contest. It could send a priest whose preaching would cut conquest gains in the Barrens by 20%. Assessors found that past Imperial massacres and the deaths of rebel leaders mean no effective uprising is possible for ten years. That could be shortened by the Winter Sun breaking chains, reconciling with the Great Forest Orcs, a Senate motion promising them the Heart of Peytaht, tolerating Freedom in doctrine, or the eternal Irra Harah. Dawnish, Varushkan and Highborn mandates could strengthen military units supporting the conquest.

n.Dawn: Dawn's armies led the invasion and cut the Barrens in two, but were credited with only 41.8% of the land taken. The Great Forest Orcs blame Dawn for the failed rebellion, while a Dawn mandate could give Dawnish units an extra rank when supporting Dawnish armies there.
n.Druj: The orcs of the Barrens regard Druj rule as a known horror preferable to death at Imperial hands, so no effective rebellion against the Druj is expected for ten years unless the Empire acts to rebuild trust.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly backed the contest for the Barrens, and a proposed mandate would give Highborn military units an extra rank when supporting Dawnish or Highborn armies there.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' bid for the Barrens sparked the contest, and their Assembly vowed loyalty to allies over the challenge. Their Winter Sun army could cut a year from the wait for rebellion for each season it spends breaking chains in the Barrens.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a Dawn Assembly mandate urged Dawnish captains to stop raiding Jotun-held Skallahn and turn east to the Barrens.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs and Montanians who fled the Barrens were granted rights to live in Therunin and remain close allies of the Navarr.
n.The League: League forces were credited with 12.9% of Barrens land taken. The League's earlier award of Holberg, after Dawn had fought to liberate it, was cited as a warning that the Senate decides who receives conquered land.
n.Varushka: Driven chiefly by the Golden Axe, Varushkan forces were credited with 45.3% of land taken, and the Varushkan Assembly urged its people to fight alongside Dawn. A mandate could give Varushkan units an extra rank, and Varushkan armies would escape the General Assembly's penalty unless it passed with a greater majority.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's long ties to Sermersuaq were cited as an example of a moral claim to a territory that carries no legal right.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs long to return to their homes in the Forest of Peytaht, which spans the Barrens and Casinea.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg was cited as the city Dawn bled to liberate, only for the Senate to give it to the League.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan priests urged repaying Dawn for standing with Varushka in Ossium.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq was used as an example of Wintermark's moral rather than legal claim to a territory.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish military captains were urged to give up raiding Skallahn in favour of conquering the Barrens.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Prince-Bishop's mandate told the Empire to 'remember Skarsind' as a lesson against treating territories as prizes.
t.The Barrens: Imperial armies hold two central regions of the Barrens, but its orc inhabitants are bitterly hostile to the Empire and leaderless. Civil servants judge that no effective uprising against the Druj is possible for ten years unless the Empire acts to speed reconciliation.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Therunin is home to the Great Forest Orcs and Montanians who fled the Barrens after the failed rebellion.

r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: A Senate motion promising the Heart of Peytaht and its valuable weirwood grove to the Great Forest Orcs once the Barrens is taken was proposed. Such a motion would ease their fears and cut a year from the wait for an effective rebellion.

The power behind our moves.d: Freeborn corsairs led the seaborne evacuation along the coast, while Imperial Orc and Dawn units, with Commonwealth soldiers, reached families in the hinterland. Grendel patrols were bought off with bribes until it was too late. A furious Rahab closed Oran to Imperial ships and the border with the Brass Coast, and ordered Imperial fleets and units in Feroz harassed. He now faces ruinous costs buying slaves. The High Council did not treat the treaty as broken. It declared its slave-release obligation discharged and demanded the six wains of weirwood by the end of the Summer Solstice. Taxes from Madruga and Segura rose. Several great works were proposed, and a conjunction was offered to stop a Grendel raid into Segura.

n.Dawn: Dawnish military units, together with the Imperial Orcs, provided the bulk of the forces that slipped past Grendel patrols to rescue families from the hinterland of Morajasse and Afarjasse.
n.Grendel: The Grendel lost tens of thousands of workers from Feroz, and Governor Rahab must now buy slaves from Dubhtraig at ruinous cost. The High Council rebuffed his call for war but demanded the weirwood owed by the Empire, warning that failure to pay by the end of the Summer Solstice would breach the treaty.
n.Imperial Orcs: A quarter of all the military units in the hinterland operation were Imperial Orc, so many that one Freeborn observer wondered whether the entire nation had come to help people escape.
n.Navarr: Navarr contributed fleets to the evacuation, and the in-character tale celebrates a lone Navarr who guided Freeborn to safety across the border as a symbol of friendship between the nations.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn fleets made up more than half of the armada, to great national pride, and the evacuees settled mostly in Madruga and Segura, bringing wealth and expertise. Freeborn units and fleets still based in Feroz now face active Grendel harassment.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark sent ships to the evacuation, with Navarr, Wintermark and the League together providing nearly sixty fleets.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: corsairs remarked that with this many fleets behind the Freeborn Storm the Empire might still be contesting the Bay, and the treaty bars new shipyards or navies on it.
t.Feroz: Almost all of the Freeborn population was evacuated from Feroz. Rahab closed the port of Oran and the border, and Imperial fleets and military units based there now suffer the conquered territory penalty.
t.Madruga: Most evacuees settled in Madruga, raising its taxes by 30 thrones a season. Vintners from Fontargenta are founding vineyards, and opportunities arose to rebuild the Atalaya shipyards, found a School of Naval Warfare at Calvos and build the Parador of Sand and Salt at Quzar.
t.Segura: Evacuees swelled Segura's towns and raised its taxes by 20 thrones a season. Spice Garden workers will upgrade its herb gardens, and a column of Grendel Wave Riders has crossed its border to raid a Freeborn parador.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Few but hard-to-reach families in the Afarjasse hinterland were rescued by military units, and a quest into the Afar Hills freed two Zemress islanders from the orc garrison at Mora's Rock.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Freeborn of the conquered Cazar Straits, who had been forbidden to leave, were smuggled out in the evacuation.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Freeborn in conquered Fontargenta were evacuated, including a consortium of vintners who fled to establish new vineyards in Madruga.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Military units slipped past Grendel patrols to evacuate families from the Morajasse hinterland, including workers from the Spice Gardens and the offices of the Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The conquered Freeborn of Oranseri were evacuated, among them the Cereva family, who escaped Captain Dubha's household with much of his treasure and provoked a Grendel raid in pursuit.
r.Segura/Iron Plains: Former Spice Gardens head gardener Tariq i Cotarez i Guerra has proposed building the Viridian Glasshouse in the Iron Plains, which would supply herbs across Segura and re-establish the Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: The Cereva have taken sanctuary at a parador near Cerevado, and Captain Dubha's Wave Riders are closing in. A conjunction offers Imperial heroes the chance to intercept them before a bloodbath.

The sweetest of songs.d: The Senate's free trade pact with Sumaah, the Commonwealth and Axos boosted fleets trading there but cost the treasury. Its embargo on Jarm led the House of Princes to outlaw trade with Imperials, closing the Pallas Docks and emptying the Jarmish Lodge. The Thule Dragons freed all slaves, sought recompense for storm damage and completed Eldfell in Miechernya. Faraden's new Liege ended foreign slavery and offered the Gloaming Road as an Imperial title. Sarcophan offered port access in return for free trade. Mathilda Fisher was coming to seek a treaty for a 'Free Bregas'. Kaliact finished two Spiral forts with Jarmish help, and Asavea fell silent.

n.Dawn: Lord Colwynn de Rondell, Dawn's Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, was due to meet the Suranni envoy Ser Pippin at Anvil, and the Modnos price on his heart was rescinded.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the page only alludes to the malign force at the centre of Spiral, against which the Grendel trade protective building knowledge.
n.Grendel: Governor Rahab of Feroz remained furious and was shipping in slaves from Tathar at his own expense. Salt Lord Kaliact kept Spiral's freedoms and finished Suilven and the walled Palace of Apulian, apparently with Jarmish magicians' enchantments.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc prisoners in Faraden would be freed or allowed to seek ransom like other foreigners rather than handed to the Jotun, and Ashborn Pakt of the Imperial Orcs remained Ambassador to Asavea.
n.Jotun: Mathilda Fisher came with the backing of the Jotun of Narkyst to seek Bregasland's neutrality, failing which a Jotun invasion of Mitwold and Mournwold was likely. The Jotun also paid off the debts of orcs enslaved in Faraden and took them into their hands.
n.The League: Erasmo di Tassato, the League's Ambassador to Faraden, was praised by the Faraden and arranged restitution over Moonwater Hall. League cities felt Jarm's trade ban and the Sarcophan enclave in Sarvos.
n.The Marches: The Marcher assembly rejected Mathilda Fisher's claim to Bregasland, where the Strong Reeds and House Greywater still resisted. Yet households in Mitwold and the western Mourn feared the Jotun invasion that refusing a treaty might bring.
n.Thule: The Dragons freed all Thule slaves and expected the Senate to lift sanctions, though their caste society was otherwise unchanged. They sought recompense for storm-damaged mines, completed Eldfell and offered to trade at the Winter Markets.
n.Urizen: Urizen citizens paid to weave mithril nets into Kaliact's Spiral fortifications reported Jarmish magicians enchanting them. Some in Urizen suggested the Marchers should also give up land for peace.
n.Varushka: Varushkans remaining in Miechernya were forced to pay heavy taxes to their new Thule overlords, though some lowlanders were curious about the orcs' trade. Yevgeni Katzev of Varushka remained Ambassador to Otkodov.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark artisans still enslaved by the Thule were freed and were being sent back over the border, and the fort of Eldfell now secured the eastern end of what Wintermark called Wulfric's Fall.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: ships in the Bay reported vessels carrying many slaves from Fort Fuil into Feroz.
t.Bregasland: The Jotun-backed 'Steward' Mathilda Fisher sought Senate recognition of Bregasland as a neutral 'Free Nation of Bregas', while the Strong Reeds and House Greywater fought on against the invaders.
t.Feroz: With most Freeborn evacuated, Governor Rahab was importing slaves from Tathar at great personal expense to replace their labour.
t.Karsk: The Solstice storms ravaged the Thule-held region of Krevsaty, damaging orc farms and mines.
t.Miekarova: The Thule completed the fortification of Eldfell in Miechernya, and their settlers taxed the remaining Varushkans while offering to trade at the Winter Markets.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold faced the prospect of Jotun invasion if no treaty over Bregasland was secured.
t.Mournwold: The western Mourn feared Jotun attack: Meade lay within striking distance of Gravenmarch, and the orcs of Green March dreaded a return to thralldom.
t.Ossium: The magical storms struck the Thule-held regions of Bonewood and Webwood, harming orc farms and mines.
t.Otkodov: The Thule of Otkodov promised to welcome Imperial merchants if the Senate lifted its sanctions, and the new fort of Eldfell overlooked the passes into their land.
t.Sarvos: The Sarcophan enclave at the old Alivetti Estates prospered but gained a reputation for licentiousness, with drugs and services sold that troubled some priests and magistrates.
t.Sermersuaq: The storms ravaged the Thule-held Silver Peaks, damaging orc settlements, farms and mines.
t.Skarsind: The storms ravaged Thule-held Crow's Ridge, adding to the orcs' complaints about damage to their mines.
t.Spiral: Salt Lord Kaliact kept the people of Spiral's freedoms and completed the fortified Palace of Apulian and Suilven in six months, apparently with Jarmish enchantments.
t.Tassato: Tassato's streets were flooded, and Jarm's trade ban emptied the Jarmish Lodge there and reduced the mana reaching the Tassato Mana Exchange.
t.Tathar: Mentioned in passing: Fort Fuil in Tathar was the source of the slaves being shipped into Feroz.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Mentioned in passing: Gravenmarch is named as lying within striking distance of Meade should the Jotun advance.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: The Thule-held Krevsaty was among the regions ravaged by the Solstice storms, harming its farms and mines.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: The Thule finished building Eldfell here, overlooking the passes to Otkodov. Their settlers taxed the remaining Varushkans harshly while offering ore, mana and furs for food at the Winter Markets.
r.Mournwold/Green March: The orcs of Green March feared that a Jotun invasion would return them to thralldom under their former masters.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The storms ravaged Thule-held Bonewood, damaging orc farms and mines.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The storms ravaged Thule-held Webwood, damaging orc farms and mines.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The storms hit the Thule-held Silver Peaks hard, though the Thule seers expected a crop of magical healing herbs to follow.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Crow's Ridge suffered storm damage to its Thule settlements, part of the grievance over which the Thule sought Senate recompense.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Salt Lord Kaliact completed the fortification of Suilven in Ossuary, guarding the southern end of the Twilight Gate, probably with Jarmish magic.
r.Tassato/Enterio: Mentioned in passing: Enterio is not named; the page touches Tassato only through its flooded streets and the Jarmish Lodge and Mana Exchange losses.

There is thunder.d: Chalonsio, ruled from the Sapphire Keep by Patricio Sebastian Ceruleo, handles most foreign slaves entering Asavea. Its Chain District holds the Grand Temple of the God of Chains, where the priesthood was gathering. The Sumaah aimed to free slaves, sink slavers and destroy the markets and temple. The Commonwealth pledged only limited ships. Without Senate action, Imperial participation would be illegal. The raid's outcome would depend on how much Imperial strength joined, with rewards and plunder on offer but a likely collapse in Asavean relations. A mountebank proposed that the Ambassador to Asavea secretly warn Lady Madriannia of the Blue Stones instead, at great risk to the Liberty Pact.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the current Ambassador to Asavea, the only person Lady Madriannia would believe if warned of the raid, is Ashborn Pakt of the Imperial Orcs, though the title was up for election.
n.The Brass Coast: Sumaah enthusiasm for the raid was strengthened by the example of Zemress, the Blade of the Isles, and the former pirates leading the attack hoped to fight beside Imperial citizens who follow her path.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Asavean shipping along the Bay of Catazar had fallen to an all-time low amid worsening relations and mutual sanctions.
t.Madruga: Sumaah visitors to the Zemress Seminary in Madruga were credited with strengthening support for the plan to strike at Chalonsio.

This little light of mine.d: The Citadel Guard, Eastern Sky, Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave, Towerjacks and Fist of the Mountain, bolstered by Autumn and Day magic, clashed with Druj armies that were bent on slaughter and empowered by Spring magic. The Empire narrowly prevailed, but more than 2,500 Imperial soldiers died and Clypion's eastern spires stayed in Druj hands. Survivors and refugees joined the Citadel Guard. Zenith's trods collapsed, and Proceris gained the Nightwoven quality. The Solstice battle offered a chance to kill Karvor Eyepeel and seize Clypion, and to kill his tepel to weaken Iteri. Conjunctions targeted a stolen magical text, the Druj champion Khelver and the Amulet of Truth, and two groups of mysteriously afflicted former prisoners.

n.Dawn: The Eastern Sky, under its new General Dame Aurum De Castellan, led the assault in Clypion, and Aurum's virtuous auras inspired Zenith's survivors. Yeomen of Dawn were among the emptied former prisoners at the Grove of the Halls.
n.Druj: The Druj matched the Empire's numbers but favoured slaughter over holding ground, and they were narrowly driven east. Their leader in Zenith, Karvor Eyepeel, was left trapped in a salient at Mount Ossa and exposed to an Imperial strike.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar and Seventh Wave fought on their Virtuous Crusade in Zenith. A conjunction offered the chance to slay Khelver and recover the Amulet of Truth stolen from Tabernacle, which would make both armies unbreakable while they stayed in Zenith.
n.Navarr: The trods of Zenith collapsed, possibly through Druj action, so the Dance of Navarr and Thorn would need to be performed again. Some vates doubted whether restoring them from Anvil was wise.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard, swelled by 1,000 Urizeni recruits who would desert if the campaign faltered, helped push the Druj back in Clypion. The surviving Urizen of the territory began to come out of hiding to fight for their home.
n.Wintermark: The Fist of the Mountain marched across the Empire to join the fight and helped turn the tide in Clypion. Wintermark war scout Kefry Lanesson sought aid for emptied former prisoners, some of them Wintermarkers.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Druj champion Khelver is described as a veteran of the war in Casinea.
t.Hahnmark: The grimnir of Kronehal in Hahnmark promised herbs, including true vervain, for every afflicted former prisoner saved, since some of them hail from their Hall.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Fist of the Mountain marched from Kallavesa to Zenith, guided by Autumn magic.
t.Morrow: The Druj sought to rout the Imperial armies back into Morrow. An Imperial victory at the Solstice might inspire Morrow's spires to help drive the Druj from Iteri.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: a clear victory might inspire the spires of Redoubt to help retake Zenith.
t.Reikos: The Amulet of Truth sought in Zenith was stolen by Khelver from the Tabernacle museum in Reikos, where he slew its last curator. The ruined museum has since been swallowed by Llofir's magic.
t.Sarangrave: Druj reinforcements marched out of the Sarangrave's forests into Zenith. Vikari serving the ghulai Cintra Blackstaff were bearing a stolen text back there.
t.Zenith: The Empire narrowly pushed the Druj back but still lacked a beachhead. The territory remained Terrorised and under miasma, its trods collapsed, and a Solstice battle offered the chance to cut it in two.

r.Hahnmark/Kronemark: Prosperous grimnir of Kronehal pledged a true vervain and another herb for each of their afflicted folk saved from the Grove of the Halls.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: The text looted from the Spire of Sleet was being carried to the Palace of the Sleepers in Kroll, unless Imperial heroes intercepted it.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Imperial armies came nine-tenths of the way to capturing Clypion, though its eastern spires stayed with the Druj. Killing Karvor Eyepeel at the Solstice would collapse the Mount Ossa salient and take the region.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Taking Clypion would isolate Iteri. Each of Karvor's tepel killed and looted would cut the victory points needed to take Iteri, provided the Empire attacks it next season.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The Druj kept a familiar Spring-magic fortification over Lustri's woods. A conjunction to Sleetstorm Pass in south-western Lustri offered a chance to recover the stolen text.
r.Zenith/Proceris: A Druj labyrinth of rotting wood and mist rose around the ruined Golden Cascade, and Proceris permanently gained the Nightwoven quality. Conjunctions there concerned Khelver and the looted Spire of Sleet.

To ride the earth.d: Six Imperial armies were pressing into Zenith. Urizeni volunteers answering the Assembly's call added a thousand to the Citadel Guard's strength. Because Cardinal of Loyalty Veikko Bondforger rallied the faithful, Urizen's spires and temples committed supplies, so the Guard faces no supply problems until the end of Summer 385YE, provided no region of Redoubt or Morrow is lost. The General Assembly could tithe liao from every congregation to negate the Druj miasma in Zenith for a season and make Imperial armies there unbreakable. Following Clytemnestra's unanimously upheld statement, the Urizen Assembly may enact a mandate disbanding the Citadel Guard while any part of Zenith remains in Druj hands.

n.Dawn: Dawnish armies were fighting alongside Urizen and Highguard in Zenith and would benefit from the proposed General Assembly mandate. Urizeni also feared armies might be called north to conquer new territories for Dawn.
n.Druj: The Druj face six Imperial armies in Zenith. If the General Assembly mandate passes, their miasma would have no effect there for a season, and Imperial armies fighting them would become unbreakable.
n.Grendel: Salt Lord Kaliact's détente had kept the Citadel Guard supplied, but Urizen no longer needs that deal for the coming year. This may weaken the Salt Lord's leverage in further negotiations with the Empire.
n.Highguard: The Highborn crusade continued in Zenith: the Valiant Pegasus withdrew to Bastion to resupply, while the Granite Pillar and Seventh Wave kept attacking and inspired those who witnessed them.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni feared Imperial armies might be called west to face the Jotun before Zenith was freed.
n.Urizen: Loyalty-driven volunteers and supplies strengthened the Citadel Guard and secured its supply for a year. Meanwhile, Clytemnestra's unanimous statement gave the Urizen Assembly the option of disbanding the Guard if the Empire abandons Zenith.
n.Varushka: The proposed General Assembly mandate would only take its liao tithe from Varushka, and only make Varushkan armies unbreakable, if it passed with a greater majority. Urizeni also feared armies being diverted to conquests for Varushka.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark armies had come to Zenith to aid Urizen and Highguard and would gain the proposed mandate's protection against the miasma.

t.Bastion: The Highborn army the Valiant Pegasus pulled back to Bastion to resupply before continuing the crusade.
t.Morrow: The Citadel Guard's year of secure supply depends on no region of Morrow being lost.
t.Redoubt: The Citadel Guard's guaranteed supply until the end of Summer 385YE depends on no region of Redoubt being lost.
t.Spiral: Grendel-held Spiral's détente with the Empire had kept the Citadel Guard supplied, but that deal ends at the Summer Solstice and Urizen no longer needs it for the coming year.
t.Zenith: Six Imperial armies were pushing the Druj back in Zenith. A proposed mandate could negate the miasma there for a season and make Imperial armies unbreakable while fighting in the territory.

r.Zenith/Lustri: Mentioned in passing: Clytemnestra's statement asks whether the Senate might leave the spires of Lustri in Druj hands.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Mentioned in passing: named among the Zenith regions Urizeni fear the Senate might leave under Druj control.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Mentioned in passing: its spires are cited in Clytemnestra's warning against abandoning Zenith to the Druj.

Two steps on the water.d: The Free Folk, guests of the House of the Proffered Hand, work across the Empire, especially in the Marches, and venerate statues of a 'Divine Family' including unknown figures such as Truthful Alexio and Tajlora the Wise. Conservative priests call this idolatry and heresy; the Synod was asked for statements of principle, particularly in the Assembly of the Nine, General Assembly or Dawnish assembly. Hostile judgements would likely lead them to seek homes elsewhere rather than to violence. Meanwhile the Marracossans, led in negotiations by Leonorada Rousseau, proposed that the Senate cede Trajadoz in return for a Bourse-appointed Marracossa Sendito with a ministry selling unique talismans. Legate Glaucia Herminia planned to visit Anvil to speak with the Ambassador to Asavea.

n.Dawn: Dawn hosts the Free Folk in Astolat; yeofolk largely see them as 'a little weird', but the Dawnish national assembly was named as a suitable place for a statement of principle on whether their faith should be tolerated.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Pakt of the Imperial Orcs was noted as the incumbent Ambassador to Asavea whom the Marracossan Legate hoped to meet.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: visiting Free Folk mistook the statues at the House of Barbs in Hercynia for unknown exemplars.
n.The Brass Coast: The Marracossans live as foreigners in Madruga, employing Freeborn labourers and clashing with Freeborn honesty through their habits of discreet bribery; they asked that the Marracossa Sendito be appointed via the Bourse, possibly as a Freeborn national position.
n.The Marches: Many Free Folk worked as fair-waged labourers in the Marches, and planned to visit the Marches camp at Anvil to share delicacies with 'the distant cousins of our distant cousins'.

t.Astolat: The Free Folk have begun building homes in Astolat, where local troubadours and faithful sought clarity on how to treat them amid fears of 'another Whittle'.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Free Folk visiting the House of Barbs in Hercynia were confused, taking its statues for images of unknown exemplars.
t.Madruga: The Marracossans resettled the abandoned town of Trajadoz in northern Madruga, restoring farms and workshops, and requested that the Senate cede it to them.
t.Mitwold: Many Free Folk travelled to Mitwold seeking farm and outdoor labour, sharing stories and their faith after work.
t.Upwold: Free Folk visited Upwold in numbers to work fields, orchards and building projects for a fair wage.

r.Madruga/Torres: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named directly, though the Marracossans' settlement at Trajadoz lies in northern Madruga.

Wake up crying.d: At least thirty miners are believed dead and forty seriously injured. The tainted water leaves people listless or ill-tempered and corrodes metal, wood and structures. Fennir of Brackenbeak Hall still receives this season's 7 rings of ilium, but the mine may produce nothing afterwards. The Senate could invest in a rune-forged refit proposed by Holberg engineers, which would raise output by 2 rings. It could instead pay 10 Thrones to reopen the mine at a higher upkeep, or do nothing and accept upkeep of 15 Thrones. The Silver Chalice could heal Syrene with 50 crystal mana, and miners sought Synod guidance. Regrow the Land's Heart could not help that season.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: because the Scorrero Nets are in Grendel hands, experienced workers used to dangerous waters are available to work Syrene's Wisdom if the Senate does nothing.
n.Highguard: Highborn miners and the townsfolk of Syrene suffered deaths, injuries and lost homes. Grieving families turned to the Synod for a statement on whether such dangerous work can ever be fairly recompensed.
n.The League: A cadre of Holberg engineers diverted to Syrene and proposed an expensive rune-forged refit of the Lady Isabella pump. Their plan would make the mine safer and more productive.

t.Casinea: Casinea's town of Syrene was devastated by tainted floodwater and a mudslide that washed out the roads to Anvil. Its chapters allied in relief, aided by draughir and briar-born volunteers who were unaffected by the taint, while the mine itself remained a flooded death trap.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the engineers who offered the refit plan for Syrene's Wisdom came from Holberg, on their way to visit the Silent Sentinel.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: the proposed refit would draw on techniques developed when the Great Pits of Ennerlund were improved against flooding from the Morass.

What's good for me.d: The Jarmish House of Princes extended its ultimatum but asked the Senate to reassure them and urge the Commonwealth towards diplomacy. If it did not, ties would be severed. The Thule invited the Ambassador to Otkodov to a caucus forum meeting and asked for 120 crystal mana. Asavean families warned the Cavabianca Docks would close unless the Empire raised a statue or made a statement supporting the Plenum. Mathilda Fisher and the Jotun asked the Empire to cede or abandon Bregasland. Salt Lord Kaliact began two fortifications in Spiral and will renegotiate Urizen support for the Citadel. The Suranni sought help capturing fleeing Hand of Dumon members, while the Hand begged the Conclave for sanctuary.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a quoted Marches Assembly judgement recalls that the Marchers left Dawn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: they are named as an enemy of the Thule alliance, whose Ossium garrison has fought them.
n.Grendel: Salt Lord Kaliact is building two fortifications in Spiral and will renegotiate the Urizen arrangement there. The North Mareave Trading Consortium is buying 50 wains each of weirwood and white granite at reduced prices, and Grendel are courting the Asavean granite trade for Dubhtraig.
n.Highguard: Highguard fleets would suffer a 1 rank trade penalty if the Senate agreed to the Suranni request. Unlike Freeborn and League ships, they would get no benefit from a reopened Robec.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Asavea, Ashborn Pakt, is of the Imperial Orcs.
n.Jotun: The Jotun back Mathilda Fisher's bid to complete the conquest of Bregasland and would recognise it as a free nation. Without a treaty, they would likely support her by invading Mitwold and Mournwold; meanwhile the Thule fight them in Sermersuaq.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the new Ambassador to Jarm, Gelert Ashborn, is Navarr and secured the extension of the Jarmish ultimatum.
n.The Brass Coast: Commonwealth zauberer have joined the Lyceum Schloss in Madruga. The Suranni proposal would mean a 1 rank trade penalty for Freeborn fleets, followed by a reopened Robec with a trade bonus; Fleet Master Ezro remains ambassador to the Grendel.
n.The League: Sarvos risks losing the Cavabianca Docks unless the Empire mends ties with the Asavean Plenum. A Jarmish break would cut mana to the Tassato Mana Exchange, and League fleets face the same Suranni penalty and potential Robec bonus as the Freeborn.
n.The Marches: Mathilda Fisher, whom the Marches Assembly has condemned, demands that the Empire cede the rest of Bregasland. Refusal is likely to bring a Jotun invasion of Mitwold and Mournwold.
n.Thule: The Thule maintain their military alliance, fighting in Sermersuaq and defending Ossium. They have booked Lashonar's caucus forum to discuss the campaigns with the Ambassador to Otkodov and to receive 120 crystal mana (or quintessence).
n.Urizen: Urizen in Spiral are building mithril nets into the Grendel fortifications, and Salt Lord Kaliact wants an offer for allowing them to keep supporting the Citadel. Urizen fleets would face the Suranni-related trade penalty, and Tarquinius Ankarien remains Ambassador to Axos.
n.Varushka: The Thule garrison in Ossium has defended the Varushkan territory against the Druj. The Thule have also finished consolidating the lands ceded to them under the Winter treaty.
n.Wintermark: Thule armies continue to fight beside Imperial forces liberating Sermersuaq from the Jotun. Eska Crowspeaker of Wintermark, as Voice of Liberty, holds the outcome of the Liberty Pact meeting.

t.Bay of Catazar: Sarcophan merchants trade throughout the Bay's ports, and the Commonwealth fleet has left it. The Suranni propose that magistrates along the Bay help capture fleeing Hand of Dumon members.
t.Bregasland: Mathilda Fisher and the Jotun hold three-fifths of the territory and intend to finish the conquest this season. They ask the Empire to cede the rest or withdraw its armies so an independent Bregasland can be agreed by treaty.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to the recent evacuation of Feroz, aided by the Muffled Oar ritual and Commonwealth ships, and notes the harsh treatment of the few people left under the Grendel.
t.Madruga: Commonwealth zauberer, including Professor Michael Enden of Volkavaar, have settled at the Lyceum Schloss and founded a popular battle-magic duelling club.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the North Mareave Trading Consortium, which backs the Mountains of the Moon raid, is buying weirwood and white granite from Imperial traders.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: the Thule have completed consolidation of lands ceded to them under the Winter treaty.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold faces a likely Jotun invasion if no treaty over Bregasland is secured with Mathilda Fisher.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: the North Mareave Trading Consortium is said to back Paymaster Muireall's plan to raid the Mountains of the Moon.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold faces a likely Jotun invasion if no treaty over Bregasland is secured with Mathilda Fisher.
t.Ossium: The Thule garrison here has fought off the Druj, the Thule have completed consolidation of the Webwood, and they want to discuss the Ossium campaign at the caucus forum.
t.Otkodov: The Thule invite the Ambassador to Otkodov, Yevgeny Katzev, and two companions to the caucus forum to coordinate the alliance's military campaigns.
t.Redoubt: The Senate commissioned an embassy with the Grendel at Cargo in Redoubt, but no progress has yet been made on it.
t.Sarvos: The Cavabianca Docks will stop trading after the Summer Solstice unless relations with the Plenum improve. The Asavean families suggest a statue of Balo of the Foam or Lord Isso; a larger one would add a third rank to the docks.
t.Segura: Segura borders the Suranni territory of Arbonne. Baroness Katerine asks that its magistrates and militia help Suranni law enforcement capture fleeing Hand of Dumon members.
t.Sermersuaq: Thule armies continue to fight alongside Imperial forces to liberate Sermersuaq from the Jotun, and the campaign is to be discussed at the caucus forum.
t.Spiral: Salt Lord Kaliact is raising two fortifications, sped by Autumn magic and due before the Autumn Equinox. She will renegotiate the Urizen arrangement there but promises no change before then.
t.Tassato: Mathilda Fisher's emissary came to the Imperial Consulate in Tassato. A break with Jarm would also reduce the mana available to the Tassato Mana Exchange.

r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Imperial armies still hold Ottermire, which Mathilda Fisher intends to conquer unless the Empire cedes it or withdraws.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: Imperial armies still hold the Rushes, which Mathilda Fisher intends to conquer unless the Empire cedes it or withdraws.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mentioned in passing: the page notes only that the Thule have completed consolidation of Miekarovan lands ceded to them by the Winter treaty.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The Thule have completed their consolidation of the Webwood, ceded to them by the Senate in the Winter treaty.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The Salt Lord is building great walls and a fortified palace at Apullian, using mithril nets worked by Urizen. The North Mareave Trading Consortium's representative is also based here.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: A Grendel fortification is rising at the southern end of the Twilight Gate in Ossuary, magically accelerated and due before the Autumn Equinox.
